Latest Update: Liverpool transfer news: Virgil van Dijk 'succession' plan revealed as Andoni Iraola targets £50m Bundesliga defender

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (344 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Lewis Nolan | 25 Nov 2026 23:55.
  • Liverpool are seriously considering re-signing Jarell Quansah from Bayer Leverkusen in 2027, the latest report has claimed.
  • Andoni Iraola's side emerged as 3-0 winners against Club Brugge in the Champions League on Wednesday, with the Merseysiders keeping a second consecutive clean sheet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Nolan | 25 Nov 2026 23:55.

Liverpool are seriously considering re-signing Jarell Quansah from Bayer Leverkusen in 2027, the latest report has claimed.

Andoni Iraola's side emerged as 3-0 winners against Club Brugge in the Champions League on Wednesday, with the Merseysiders keeping a second consecutive clean sheet.

Captain Virgil van Dijk started on the bench, before coming on to add more solidity at the back alongside Jeremy Jacquet.

Van Dijk has been exceptional once again this season, but with his contract set to expire at the end of the current campaign, Iraola could soon be in the market for a replacement.

TEAMtalk have claimed that former Red Quansah has emerged as a serious target, though Liverpool's buy-back clause of £50m will expire after the coming summer transfer window, meaning a decision about signing him will have to be made in the coming months.

Quansah is a strong passer of the ball ane has demonstrated in the past that he is capable of coming out on top in battles in the air, though he has struggled to settle this season.

In the 2026-27 Bundesliga, the centre-back has only completed 42.3 passes per match and has won just 32% of his aerial duels, something that may be a major concern to Liverpool given he is 6ft 3in.

The 23-year-old completed 52.8 passes per game last season in the league, while he also won 60% of his aerial duels.

There are concerns about Quansah's recovery defending and temperament inside the box, so perhaps Liverpool should look elsewhere in the summer for the heir to Van Dijk.

The unfortunate reality for Liverpool is that they will have to become accustomed to life without Van Dijk sooner rather than later.

However, there is nothing to suggest based on his current form that the 35-year-old cannot continue to play at the highest level for at least another season.

As long as Van Dijk can continue to dominate attackers and use his immense recovery pace, then Liverpool should look to extend their captain's contract.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • AC Milan defender Strahinja Pavlovic will partake in further medical tests tomorrow, according to a report, to assess the problem with his kidney stone.
  • It’s been a tough season for Pavlovic where injuries are concerned.
  • Barring that, Ruben Amorim has looked to him whenever possible.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan defender Strahinja Pavlovic will partake in further medical tests tomorrow, according to a report, to assess the problem with his kidney stone.

It’s been a tough season for Pavlovic where injuries are concerned. He struggled through the first international break with fatigue and he’s since had a month-long issue with his kidney, which has kept him out of action.

Barring that, Ruben Amorim has looked to him whenever possible. So the Serbian’s absence is a major loss for the Portuguese, who has also taken to a liking to him, as Massimiliano Allegri did before him.

According to Gazzetta dello Sport, via MilanXtra on X, the Serbian defender will head for further medical tests tomorrow at La Madonnina – where medicals for newly introduced signings are normally held – to assess the issues with his kidney stones.

The problem has sidelined him throughout the past month, so it’s something that must be looked at further to avoid it becoming a recurring issue. Any outcome could also be key for the next few months, too.

Last night, Amorim mentioned Pavlovic when questioned about Goncalo Inacio. So, if the defender is to be out for much longer, he may have to revisit his own comments….

By Anthony Nolan | 26 Nov 2026 00:03.

Chelsea will travel to face relegation-threatened Nottingham Forest on Friday, desperate to push towards the European places in the Premier League table.

However, manager Xabi Alonso will be without a number of key players for the trip, while doubts remain about the fitness of Moises Caicedo and Jamie Gittens.

Emiliano Martinez is likely to start in goal, protected by a centre-back duo of Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill, who will be looking for a rare clean sheet in the absence of Maxence Lacroix, who is dealing with a hamstring injury.

Josh Acheampong should operate at right-back, while Pep Chavarria takes the left-sided role, given that Reece James is sidelined with a knee injury and Jorrel Hato has a back matter.

In midfield, Jordan Henderson and Romeo Lavia are the names in the frame to form Alonso's double pivot, considering that Caicedo was forced off in the 4-1 loss to Leeds United with back trouble.

Further forward, winger Gittens has returned to training but is still building fitness, so expect to see Pedro Neto and Morgan Rogers start on the flanks.

Talisman Cole Palmer should take the number 10 role on Friday, supporting striker Emmanuel Emegha up top while Joao Pedro recovers from a thigh injury.

Chelsea possible starting lineup:.

Martinez; Acheampong, Fofana, Colwill, Chavarria; Henderson, Lavia; Neto, Palmer, Rogers; Emegha.

#142162. Arsenal's silent flaw of switching off could bite them hard against Europe's best - it's not sustainable and they were made to pay again in Borussia Dortmund draw, writes ISAAN KHAN

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (929 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Arsenal's silent flaw of switching off could bite them hard against Europe's best - it's not sustainable and they were made to pay again in Borussia Dortmund draw, writes ISAAN KHAN

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (929 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 17:22 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Whether through complacency, boredom, or a mixture of both, Arsenal's habit of switching off in the second half of matches is becoming a serious issue.
  • It is a flaw which could bite them hard against teams they would encounter in the later stages of the Champions League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 17:22 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 24 November 2026.

Whether through complacency, boredom, or a mixture of both, Arsenal's habit of switching off in the second half of matches is becoming a serious issue.

It is a flaw which could bite them hard against teams they would encounter in the later stages of the Champions League.

When Kepa Arrizabalaga parried Julian Ryerson's shot into the path of Jobe Bellingham, the Arsenal script had seemingly flipped from first-half domination to second-half capitulation.

Luckily for Mikel Arteta, Bellingham's tap-in was flagged for offside to keep the north London club's unbeaten record in this competition intact, stretching back to 20 matches (excluding penalty shootouts).

Earlier in the second half, Maximilian Beier had equalised, skilfully turning Gabriel before placing a neat strike past Kepa.

Recent findings suggest that but this match should have been sealed well before then for Arsenal - and they had enough chances to win it late on, too. Viktor Gyokeres headed wide when unmarked and Declan Rice struck the woodwork.

Arsenal were made to pay for their complacency again by drawing with Borussia Dortmund.

Arsenal were held 1-1 with Dortmund thanks to this Maximilian Beier's strike for the visitors.

By full-time, the Gunners had mustered 30 shots, but no winning goal.

Industry observers note that despite his team's wastefulness, Arteta said: 'The domination and threat was really impressive. The general feeling inside the dressing room is that we should reward ourselves with more. I love the courage, the fluidity and the understanding with the players with and without the ball.'.

But the recurrence of losing concentration later in matches, as the Gunners did against Slavia Prague and Newcastle in recent weeks, is an matter which Arteta must urgently address.

It has been revealed that it is not sustainable, and ruined an evening initially lit up by Gyokeres' stunning strike. The Sweden striker's display reflected the fierce competition for places at Arsenal. Perform well and you have a chance of a starting spot. Anything less results in a place on the bench in the winter's cold.

Gyokeres received Noni Madueke's pass outside the area on ten minutes and Dortmund's back line completely backed off, almost pleading for him to shoot.

He obliged, cocking his right boot back to unleash a powerful strike which initially looked to be going over the bar before dipping into goalkeeper Gregor Kobel's net. It was a top-drawer finish from a man who cannot nail down a regular starting spot, despite 21 goals last season and a goal and assist in Arsenal's previous Champions League match against Slavia Prague.

It is the kind of luxury Arteta has worked towards since taking on this job seven years ago.

In a recent development, one back-up player who inspires rather less confidence is goalkeeper Kepa. No1 David Raya injured his shoulder at Newcastle and so in came his fellow Spaniard. Kepa's touches early on were cheered by the Arsenal faithful, massaging the confidence of a man who has endured the kind of calamity which is not easily erased from memory.

The dropping of Rayan Cherki's cross in March's Carabao Cup final defeat by Manchester City; his lapse to misjudge a corner and gift Real Betis a goal during pre-season - these are the sorts of errors which have Arsenal fans feeling uncomfortable whenever Raya is unavailable.

Viktor Gyokeres (left) opened the scoring with this stunning long-range strike for the Gunners.

Kepa Arrizabalaga (right) started in goal for Arsenal with first-choice David Raya out injured.

Arsenal (4-2-3-1): Arrizabalaga 6; White 6 (Timber 65, 6), Konsa 6, Gabriel 5, Hincapie 6; Lewis-Skelly 5 (Guimaraes 66, 6), Rice 7; Madueke 8, Odegaard 7, Tzolis 5 (Eze 66, 6); Gyokeres 7.

Borussia Dortmund (3-4-2-1): Kobel 6; Gadou 7, Anton 6, Schlotterbeck 6; Ryerson 6, Nmecha 6, Veerman 6, Svensson 6; Bellingham 6, Beier 7 (Guirassy 65, 6); Fabio Silva 6 (Karetsas 65, 6).

Raya is battling to return for Arsenal's huge Premier League clash against Manchester City on Sunday and the sense of panic in the days after his injury has been understandable.

Raya is so much more than just an excellent shot-stopper. His distribution is second to none: pinpoint long throws to set wingers away on counter-attacks and a highly impressive passing range, both aerially and across the floor.

Sources indicate that still, Kepa just about survived. There were jitters, like passing the ball straight to a yellow shirt on 52 minutes, which the opposition failed to punish. But he hung in there and that will have given his confidence a boost.

It has been revealed that arsenal started well, Madueke continuing his excellent form of late in place of the injured Bukayo Saka. Madueke crossed for Christos Tzolis, who drove his shot into the turf, before setting up Martin Odegaard to shoot wide.

It didn't take long for the winger's passing to produce results, as he fed Gyokeres for that venomous strike from distance.

Rice lashed a strike from range which dipped just over the bar as Dortmund showed a tendency to gift too much time on the ball.

After the break Dortmund changed tack. Sitting back and soaking up the pressure was not working, so they got the ball forward more swiftly and more often, forcing Arsenal on to the back foot.

The Gunners held on for a point - and endured another lesson in switching off.

This evening, AC Milan have been dealt some good and bad injury news ahead of their game against Olympiacos.

It’s been a particularly unfortunate season for Milan where injuries are involved, and today, they have suffered a new problem in midfield, with Luka Modric out of this week’s crucial game in the Europa League.

In a recent development, milanNews relays a report from Sky, and it’s best to start with the bad news: Modric has suffered ‘a muscle strain in his right rectus femoris’. The Croatian will definitely miss this week’s game against the Greek outfit and the game against Cagliari is in doubt.

However, he should be back for the game against Parma. It offers a substantial chance for Ardon Jashari to potentially step up, especially after his goal at the weekend. Nevertheless, it brings up questions about who is fit to actually replace the Croatian in the squad.

Portland Timbers vs Dallas - prediction, team news, lineups

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Joel Lefevre | 26 Nov 2026 01:21, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 01:22.
  • Needing a victory to keep their MLS season alive, the Portland Timbers will host Dallas in game two of that best-of-three series on Saturday at Providence Park.
  • The opener went to Los Toros in Frisco, 3-0, putting them one win away from the Western Conference semi-finals for the first time since 2022.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joel Lefevre | 26 Nov 2026 01:21, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 01:22.

Needing a victory to keep their MLS season alive, the Portland Timbers will host Dallas in game two of that best-of-three series on Saturday at Providence Park.

The opener went to Los Toros in Frisco, 3-0, putting them one win away from the Western Conference semi-finals for the first time since 2022.

For the second successive campaign, the Timbers face a must-win situation heading into game two of the playoffs after lacking decisiveness in the attacking third last Saturday.

Portland have not made it beyond the opening round of the playoffs since their run to the MLS Cup final in 2021, losing to New York City FC on penalties that year.

They are now 12-10-8 all-time in post-season outings, while winning just one of their last seven playoff games in normal time.

That said, Marti Cifuentes has seen his side lose just one of their last six league fixtures at Providence Park, winning those last two matches and scoring three goals both times.

In addition to that, this club have gone on to win their last two post-season matches at home, while suffering just one playoff defeat this decade at Providence Park in 90 minutes.

The Timbers have never lost a playoff home game versus Dallas in normal time, though their last post-season win against them at Providence Park occurred in 2015 (3-1).

After a cagey opening 45 minutes in game one, Dallas took command in the second half last week, putting themselves in the driver’s seat to advance.

Whatever Eric Quill is saying to this group at half-time, the message has been well received, with his team outscoring opponents by a combined 6-1 margin in the second half of their last two games.

A triumph on Saturday would snap a three-match MLS winless run for the Texas club away from home and mark their first playoff victory as the visitors since beating the Timbers on penalties in Portland in 2020.

Since that triumph, Dallas have failed to score in four of their last five post-season affairs which took place outside of Frisco.

In 2026, they have conceded in all but three MLS road outings, while allowing three or more goals on four separate occasions.

Los Toros can extend their winning run versus Portland to three matches on Saturday, while they are unbeaten in eight successive meetings against them.

Portland Timbers Major League Soccer form:.

Dallas Major League Soccer form:.

Do not expect to see Juan David Mosquera on the field for the Timbers Saturday as he recovers from a foot and ankle problem, while Zac McGraw has a sore back, Brandon Bye is dealing with a knee injury and Alex Bonetig is doubtful due to a shoulder strain.

Cole Bassett and Kristoffer Velde were the most dangerous Portland players in game one, each with three shots, while James Pantemis made five stops in a losing effort.

At Dallas, Anderson Julio is questionable for this match because of a lower-body injury after sitting out in the opening game of this series.

Joaquin Valiente registered his first career playoff brace in game one, with Sam Sarver scoring his first MLS post-season goal in that victory.

Portland Timbers possible starting lineup:.

Pantemis; Hernandez, K. Miller, Waterman, Fory; Bassett, Chara, Da Costa; Velde, Janssen, Lassiter.

Dallas possible starting lineup:.

Daniel; Johansson, Urhoghide, Moore, Norris; Valiente, Kaick, Ramiro, Binyamin; Musa, Sarver.

Dallas tend to sit back away from home, and while their defensive shape will be tough to break down, we believe the Timbers' attacking depth and desperation will keep them alive.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Joel Lefevre | 26 Nov 2026 01:29, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 19:59.
  • For the first time in club history, St Louis City can advance beyond the opening round of the MLS playoffs with a victory over Los Angeles FC on Saturday at BMO Stadium.
  • Game one of this best-of-three series went the way of St Louis, who hung on to a 3-2 triumph at home on Monday night.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joel Lefevre | 26 Nov 2026 01:29, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 19:59.

For the first time in club history, St Louis City can advance beyond the opening round of the MLS playoffs with a victory over Los Angeles FC on Saturday at BMO Stadium.

Game one of this best-of-three series went the way of St Louis, who hung on to a 3-2 triumph at home on Monday night.

It was another case of too little too late for Los Angeles in game one, as they netted twice in the final 45 minutes, which was ultimately not enough.

The last six MLS goals scored by Xavi Tamarit’s men have occurred in the second half, three with fewer than 10 minutes remaining.

They enter this must-win encounter on a five-match winless run in MLS, while winning just one of their last four league games at home.

On the other hand, LAFC have only suffered one defeat in their last six league fixtures on home soil, while boasting a 100% record at BMO Stadium since the introduction of this best-of-three opening round format.

Overall, the Black and Gold have won eight playoff games at home in their history while suffering only one defeat in 11 games.

Saturday will mark the fifth time they host St Louis City with LAFC unbeaten against them at home, winning three of those matches.

The two-week break in between Decision Day and the start of the post-season seemed to do St Louis City a world of good.

Yoann Demet’s men looked a lot more like themselves than we had seen of late, winning a second successive MLS outing in game one after losing four in a row before that.

This upcoming match will only be their second playoff game away from home, after the club lost 2-1 at Sporting Kansas City in 2023.

Two of their last three domestic away matches ended in defeat, and this team have given up multiple goals on the road in seven MLS outings this year.

During the 2026 regular season, St Louis City failed to win four times away from home when netting the opening goal, though they only lost in one of those instances (3-2 at Minnesota United).

While they have yet to beat LAFC outside of Energizer Park, St Louis City have won their last two league games in California, defeating the San Jose Earthquakes and Los Angeles Galaxy during the regular season.

Los Angeles FC Major League Soccer form:.

St Louis City Major League Soccer form:.

St Louis City form (all competitions):.

Due to a pelvic matter, Timothy Tillman is questionable for Los Angeles, Jacob Shaffelburg is doubtful with a chest injury, while Thayllon and Tyler Boyd are both unlikely to feature because of leg injuries and Hugo Lloris was back between the sticks for game one.

Sergi Palencia pulled a goal back for them in St Louis the last time out, and Denis Bouanga netted a late one from the penalty spot, drawing even with Jordan Morris for the most playoff goals (11) among active MLS players.

As for St Louis, Celio Pompeu and Carlo Holse are both doubtful with knee injuries, while Roman Burki was back between the sticks in the opening game of this series.

Daniel Edelman, Jeong Sang-bin and Simon Becher all scored their first career MLS playoff goals in their game one triumph, with the latter netting with 12 minutes remaining.

Los Angeles FC possible starting lineup:.

Lloris; Palencia, Porteous, Segura, Cheberko; Choiniere, Delgado; Walta, Heung-min, Bouanga; Sieb.

St Louis City possible starting lineup:.

Burki; MacNaughton, Baumgartl, Polvara; Wallem, Durkin, Edelman, Totland; Sang-bin, Navarro, Matan.

As poor as LAFC have been, we expect their experience in these moments to shine through in game two against a St Louis City team who might take their foot off the gas, knowing they are guaranteed at least one more game no matter what.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Francesco Camarda has spoken about his Champions League goal that never was today, and how it was an AC Milan dream come true.

Camarda first became known to Milan as a youngster, but he announced himself further when he became Serie A’s youngest-ever appearance maker. He almost then went to a European level, with a goal in the Champions League. However, it wasn’t to be.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Recent findings suggest that on his debut in the competition, the starlet bagged a goal which would’ve made him the Rossoneri’s youngest-ever scorer in Europe’s main stage. Yet it was ruled out for offside and a few years on, the now 18-year-old is still waiting for a first competitive goal for the Diavolo.

Speaking to Vice, the striker opened up about his dream of playing in the Champions League at San Siro, his emotions after his goal (and it later being disallowed) and how his teammates rallied around him, as MilanVibes relayed.

It has been revealed that “As a child, I used to say to my dad: imagine if one day I could walk into San Siro and hear the Champions League anthem, accompanied by the roar of the entire stadium. When it actually happened, I thought back to that little boy and realised I had realised a dream.

“When I stepped onto the pitch, I had an incredible adrenaline rush. Then the goal came, and I felt the whole stadium explode. I also felt the affection of my teammates, who immediately raised me into the air.

“However, when I looked at the scoreboard and saw that the VAR check was in progress, I was already convinced the goal would be disallowed.

“When I returned home that evening, with my parents and cousin, I burst into tears. I was overjoyed by the goal, but at the same time deeply disappointed by what had happened. It wasn’t easy at first, but I also worked on my mental health and managed to put that moment behind me.

“Today, I’m proud of the journey I’ve taken and of having overcome those difficulties.”.

In a recent development, “I remember what Gabbia told me: he was sorry for what happened, but he explained that the experience should give me even more motivation. It should push me to improve, to train harder, and to work so I can relive even more wonderful emotions.”.

Recent findings suggest that “In football, there are positive and negative opinions; it has always been this way and will continue to be this way. A player’s true strength lies in not being influenced by what is remarked, because, regardless of whether you do well or badly, someone will always find a reason to judge you.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Joel Lefevre | 26 Nov 2026 01:34.
  • Needing a win to stay alive in the 2026 MLS Cup playoffs, the Philadelphia Union will welcome the Upcoming England Revolution to Subaru Park for game two of that opening-round series.
  • A 2-0 win at Foxborough has the Revs one triumph away from getting into the second round of the playoffs for the first time since 2021.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joel Lefevre | 26 Nov 2026 01:34.

Needing a win to stay alive in the 2026 MLS Cup playoffs, the Philadelphia Union will welcome the Upcoming England Revolution to Subaru Park for game two of that opening-round series. on Saturday.

A 2-0 win at Foxborough has the Revs one triumph away from getting into the second round of the playoffs for the first time since 2021.

More than ever, the Union must show the resilience we have seen throughout the 2026 campaign if they are to remain in the MLS playoffs.

In game one, Philly fielded the youngest starting 11 in MLS playoff history, averaging 23 years and 207 days, and that inexperience showed at times as they fired just two targeted efforts in 90 minutes.

Ryan Richter’s men have lost two of their last three league outings but have never suffered consecutive defeats since he took charge.

Since their latest coach was brought in on an interim basis, the team have won eight of their last 11 MLS games at home, with just one defeat over that stretch.

Philly have gone on to lose only one post-season outing at Subaru Park since the start of the 2022 playoffs, with Newly introduced York City FC beating them 1-0 in the conference semi-finals a year ago.

Historically, this team have never lost game two in this best-of-three playoff format, failing to concede in those two previous such outings.

A wait of over three years since their last post-season appearance was well worth it for Revs fans last weekend, who saw their team win a playoff game for the first time since 2020.

Should they triumph this weekend, they would advance beyond their first playoff opponent for the first time since 2020, when they reached the Eastern Conference Final.

New England have not won a post-season away game since then, and on Saturday can avoid suffering successive MLS away defeats for the first time since losing their first three road games of the 2026 regular season.

Marko Mitrovic is the fifth coach in club history to make the playoffs in his first season at the helm, and the Serbian can become the first Revs manager to triumph in his first MLS post-season away outing this century.

The Revs have never won game two since this best-of-three format was introduced in 2023, losing 1-0 in this exact spot at home to the Union that year.

At the same time, New England can extend their winning run versus Philly to four matches this weekend and win a playoff away game against them for the first time since 2020 (2-0).

Philadelphia Union Major League Soccer form:.

Newly introduced England Revolution Major League Soccer form:.

A concussion could keep Japhet Sery Larsen and Finn Sundstrum out of game two for the Union, while Alejandro Bedoya is questionable with an eye injury and Andre Blake is doubtful due to a groin strain.

Cavan Sullivan had a brace in their last home match of the regular season, and the promising youngster will seek his first-ever MLS playoff goal this weekend.

On the Revolution side, Griffin Yow and Leonardo Campana are both expected to miss this match with lower-body injuries.

Peyton Miller scored his career post-season goal in game one, with Nathan Harriel’s early own goal holding up as the winner, while Carles Gil picked up his sixth career postseason assist.

Philadelphia Union possible starting lineup:.

Sources indicate that rick; Westfield, Pierre, Harriel, Wagner; C. Sullivan, Jean Jacques, Lukic, Q. Sullivan; Damiani, Iloski.

Newly introduced England Revolution possible starting lineup:.

Turner; Feingold, Kohler, Wynder, Sands; Gil, Polster, Raines; Miller, Turgeman, Gazdag.

The Union have some dangerous weapons at their disposal, but overall they are on a downward trajectory, and we believe the visitors' experience will be critical in key moments on Saturday.

Carrick apology to United fans ominously similar to Solskjaer’s final match

📅 21 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 34 min read (6877 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~34 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There have been some dark days in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era but this was up there with the very worst of them: the kind of performance that gets a manager sacked, the kind of display that points to a fundamental disconnect, the kind of occasion that leaves you thinking Manchester United are as far away as they have ever been.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There have been some dark days in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era but this was up there with the very worst of them: the kind of performance that gets a manager sacked, the kind of display that points to a fundamental disconnect, the kind of occasion that leaves you thinking Manchester United are as far away as they have ever been.

When players seem so averse to doing the very basics, such as running, and the club habitually have such trouble attracting the right profiles and personalities, it is hard to escape the feeling that saying goodbye to another manager is going to do little more than paper over the many cracks at Old Trafford.

But, watching this, you had to think Michael Carrick will do well to limp on as far as Sunday, when United face Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

Industry observers note that and that was before we had heard the United captain, Bruno Fernandes, appearing to call out the manager’s tactics just a week on from the last show of public dissent from a player, when Lisandro Martínez attacked the Old Trafford board. If only these players were as good at talking on the pitch.

At the final whistle, Carrick walked over to the 700-strong group of United supporters, held up both hands in apology on no fewer than seven occasions and then walked off down the tunnel without looking in the direction of any of his players.

There were shades of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer at Watford in November 2021, when he also held up his hands in apology before being sacked 24 hours later.

In that instance, United fans booed Solskjaer. Carrick at least received some polite applause from the fans, who are a smart bunch and know the club’s problems extend far beyond the man in the dugout. Michael Carrick has insisted there is not a “toxic culture” at Manchester United in the wake of scathing criticism from former manager Erik ten Hag of the Old Trafford hierarchy and player power at the club.

The current United manager – who is under pressure after the club’s worst start to a season for 40 years – also believes he has the backing of the United board, despite Ten Hag accusing Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s Ineos regime of a series of “broken promises”.

In an interview with The Athletic, Ten Hag blamed Ratcliffe and his executives for fuelling a “toxic culture” by giving power to players and failing to back him on disciplinary matters relating to Marcus Rashford, Jadon Sancho and other first-teamers.

But Carrick said he had not encountered any toxicity since taking over from Ruben Amorim in January and suggested United’s last two outings, a 1-1 draw against Leeds United and a 2-0 defeat to Atlético Madrid, underlined the camaraderie in the group.

“Since I came back, the players and the staff have given us everything that they could give,” Carrick said before Wednesday’s Champions League clash against Cesc Fàbregas’s Como in northern Italy, where he is battling an injury and illness crisis.

“We’ve had some good performances. We’ve had some performances that we want to do better and we can improve on. We’ve made some mistakes.

Sources indicate that “But I have to say, the type of performance put into the weekend and for large parts against Atlético, there’s a lot of togetherness there. There’s a lot of will and determination to do better and wanting to do it for each other, which is important.”.

It has been revealed that good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of Manchester United’s trip to Como in the Champions League. Under normal circumstances, a visit to the idyllic Lombardy city would be a source of thrill and wonder, but Michael Carrick heads into the eye of a literal and proverbial storm at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia with his team desperately hoping to reverse their fortunes.

Absolutely tipping it down in Como, with 64mm of rain forecast before #MUFC kick-off here tomorrow ☔️ https://t.co/WvI3X8dilh.

Two wins – against Ipswich Town and Sabah – in United’s first 10 matches of the season, a public outburst from Lisandro Martínez and accusations of a “toxic culture” at the club have piled pressure on Carrick. And an uninspiring draw at Elland Road on Sunday did little to settle the rising tide of discontent within the United fanbase.

When asked for his team news, the first words that came from the United head coach’s mouth were: “Right, bit of mixed bag to be honest.” That was not a great sign, and Carrick will be without Martínez, Kobbie Mainoo, Luke Shaw, Ayden Heaven, Marcus Rashford, Benjamin Sesko and Patrick Dorgu, who are injured, while Leny Yoro serves a suspension following his red card against Atlético Madrid.

According to recent reports, like United, the hosts are without a handful of key players, with Moise Kean, Trevoh Chalobah, Assane Diao and Jesus Rodriguez missing from the match-day squad. The abundantly talented Argentine No 10 Nico Paz will feature, however, and he will be keen to showcase his talents in the Champions League.

Como have ascended from Serie B to Europe’s top table in three seasons (and from bankruptcy in nine) under Cesc Fàbregas’ watchful eye. The Spaniard is a minority owner and shareholder of the club, but as head coach he has introduced an incisive, possession-based style of play which contains hints of the managerial greats under whom he played: Arsène Wenger, Pep Guardiola, José Mourinho, Vicente del Bosque, Antonio Conte etc.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Joel Lefevre | 26 Nov 2026 01:39.
  • Charlotte FC can book a place in the second round of the MLS Cup playoffs for the first time in club history with a Saturday home win over the Chicago Fire at Bank of America Stadium.
  • A thrilling 2-1 triumph in game one last Sunday has the Crown in line to capture their first playoff series with another win this weekend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joel Lefevre | 26 Nov 2026 01:39.

Charlotte FC can book a place in the second round of the MLS Cup playoffs for the first time in club history with a Saturday home win over the Chicago Fire at Bank of America Stadium.

A thrilling 2-1 triumph in game one last Sunday has the Crown in line to capture their first playoff series with another win this weekend.

They needed to battle until the bitter end of game one, but ultimately Charlotte got the job done, scoring the winner in the 12th minute of stoppage time.

That was the first-ever playoff victory for this team in normal time, while they have never won a post-season outing at Bank of America Stadium in 90 minutes.

Coming into this upcoming match, Charlotte are unbeaten in their last four MLS affairs, while netting multiple goals in six straight domestic games.

Dean Smith’s men have not lost a single league fixture at home in 2026 when netting in the opening half, dropping points in only one of those instances all year.

This weekend they will seek a third successive MLS triumph at Bank of America Stadium and can end a two-game playoff losing run on home soil.

The Crown have netted just once in their three post-season outings at home, while conceding a combined four goals over that stretch.

Chicago have failed to keep their composure in the latter stages of matches recently, and that has them on the verge of an early playoff exit.

Gregg Berhalter’s men have conceded a stoppage-time winner in their last two MLS affairs, while allowing five goals domestically beyond 90 minutes this year.

To prolong this series to a deciding game three, they must do something they have not done in over 20 years, win a post-season match away from home, with their last one coming in 2006 at the New England Revolution (1-0).

That remarked, the Fire have won their last two league fixtures as the visitors, scoring a combined seven goals over that stretch.

They have not scored an opening-half playoff goal since a 2-0 win at home over the Revolution in the 2009 Eastern Conference Semi-finals.

On the other hand, the Fire can claim a third successive triumph at Bank of America Stadium on Saturday, blanking them 1-0 in Charlotte in September.

Charlotte FC Major League Soccer form:.

Chicago Fire Major League Soccer form:.

Lower-body injuries may keep Tim Ream, Archie Goodwin and Nimfasha Berchimas out of the lineup for Charlotte in game two, while Aron John is doubtful due to an upper-body issue.

Liel Abada and Pep Biel scored in the second half for the Crown last Sunday, with the latter netting in the dying stages of that match.

Chicago meanwhile have two players questionable in this must-win game, as Sam Rogers and Noah Allen are dealing with lower-body injuries.

Robert Lewandowski scored his first career MLS playoff goal in a losing effort, with Philip Zinckernagel collecting his third assist in as many post-season outings for the club.

Charlotte FC possible starting lineup:.

Kahlina; Byrne, Agyemang, Kessler, Toffolo; Diani, Westwood, Biel; Abada, Toklomati, Saint-Maximin.

Chicago Fire possible starting lineup:.

Brady; Dean, Elliott, Mbokazi, Gutman; Saletros, D’Avilla, Haile-Selassie; Zinckernagel, Lewandowski, Bamba.

Playoff games involving Charlotte often go down to the wire, and we believe the Crown are due to catch a break after coming oh so close to round two many times before.

Ultimately, we trust that Kristijan Kahlina can help them advance with a strong showing between the sticks.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vincenzo Montella’s time with AC Milan was ‘a dream’ for him, but he failed to achieve much during his time at the helm.

Looking back on Montella’s time leading Milan is tricky. On paper, the Italian had a strong tenure at the club, achieving a 50% win rate and only losing 18 of his 64 games in charge at San Siro, not a terrible record by any means.

According to recent reports, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Recent findings suggest that he even ended a five-year trophy drought with a win against Juventus in the Supercoppa Italiana and returned the Rossoneri to Europe, with a sixth-place finish in the 2016/17 season. In itself, that was a first since 2014.

This is where context matters, though. The start of the 2017/18 season was tough, as the Diavolo won six of their first 14 games and he was sacked before December. Despite that, he still views the club in an excellent light.

Speaking to La Gazzetta dello Sport’s ‘La Tripletta’ podcast, Montella went over his time with the club and how he fulfilled a dream by taking the job, as MilanPress relays.

In a recent development, “It was a fantastic experience there [at Milan] too, it was my dream. Then, as a professional, it’s a little different, but when I was thirteen I was a fan of that AC Milan team. My older brother took me to see Maradona’s Napoli team twice to make me a Napoli fan, and Maradona scored three goals.

In a recent development, “Despite this, my idol was Van Basten because I was a striker: I studied him and dreamed of becoming like him, and so I was a Milan fan. I knew everything about Milan, so for me it was an incredible feeling to join Milan.”.

“He liked to talk about football; he liked to give advice even when it was a bit out of context at the time, because he always had the mentality of having Van Basten as a centre forward with Papin, a two-time Ballon d’Or winner, on the bench. He wanted me to play with two strikers, and I tried to plug the gap for months.

“I told him it was difficult; I knew all the lineups of those years. I was a Milan fan: the starter was Van Basten and the reserve was Papin, both Ballon d’Or winners. So, ‘If you buy me some players like that, rest assured that I’ll play them both.'”.

“It was a year when we returned to Europe. I think it had been two or three years since Milan had been there, and it was something fresh at the time. We won a trophy, a small one. Just the other night I saw Galliani at a dinner; he reminded me of it and remembers it perfectly.

“I have to say that I found him to be the perfect manager at the time, because he was always on my side when it came to pressure; he gave me complete autonomy in my decisions and he helped me with everything, from the number of collaborators to upcoming things; whatever I asked for, he was always on the coach’s side.

“And so for me he was truly an incredible manager, who in that phase, in that change, was fundamental even in achieving these small results, especially after Berlusconi’s great AC Milan.

Industry observers note that “We deserved to win even in regulation time: we had some easy chances to win it, then it came to penalties. Gigio saved the penalty from Dybala, who kicked it really hard, but he filled the net with it.”.

“I was a little worried from the beginning because there was this obsession with publicising everything, almost like a publicity stunt, so I was a little worried. In theory, there was sharing, at least that’s what it looked like, but I couldn’t back out when in reality that wasn’t always the case.

Sources indicate that “And so sometimes there were players I hadn’t even consulted about, who would arrive and then say, ‘It was shared,’ and when you’re there, you can’t say otherwise. Certainly, when you build a team and have the budget, the first thing you do is: we had a goalkeeper, I’ll get a centre forward, we were missing a centre forward.

“In the final selection, the centre forward was the only one left, with a budget of 15-20 million. And then Kalinic… yes, I chose him because that was the final budget. So our, let’s say, second-choice striker was paid thirty-eight million, if I remember correctly, who was André Silva, and the first striker was paid half that.

“And so, in my opinion, a misunderstanding of this kind was created, with so many changes, even though at that stage we weren’t even playing badly for having fifteen upcoming players.

“We still had Calhanoglu, who wasn’t feeling well, coming off months of suspension. The team was still being built: we weren’t in line with the Scudetto objectives that had been confirmed, but certainly, given our development, we were absolutely on target.

Recent findings suggest that “Who would I have signed up front? At the time, we were probably negotiating for Aubameyang, if I remember correctly. Ronaldo? No, I didn’t believe it, not at all.”.

#142121. An extremophile transgene improves drought resistance and yield in cereals

An extremophile transgene improves drought resistance and yield in cereals

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 120 min read (23991 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~120 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Drought is a major environmental constraint limiting global crop production1,2.
  • The bulk of crop production worldwide strictly depends on rainfall to support irrigation needs, and limitations on water availability pose a global challenge for agricultural productivity, with water scarcity and drought stress incurring unpredictable and potentially catastrophic effects on yield1,2.
  • According to recent reports, conventional plant-breeding efforts have boosted crop yields in water-limited environments, for example, through improved stress resistance, greater biomass accumulation, delayed leaf senescence or ‘stay-green’ strategies7,10, but broad potential remains for improving yield and yield stability across growing regions regardless of water availability11,12.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Drought is a major environmental constraint limiting global crop production1,2. On average, crop productivity typically declines by 30–40% in moderate-drought years, whereas extreme droughts trigger far greater reductions3,4. As droughts become longer and more intense due to climate change, adverse effects on crop productivity are expected to escalate5. Breaking the trade-offs between stress resistance and yield is key to advancing crop genetic improvement as climate change sets in and the world population grows, but this is challenging for drought stress6. Here we show that heterologous expression of EpTFIIAγ, a gene encoding a transcription factor induced by osmotic stress in an extremophile lichen mycobiont, partially decouples trade-offs between stress resistance and grain production, enhancing plot yields of five wheat cultivars under water deficit by 19.4–32.8%, and per-plant yields of rice and maize by 19.7–42.4% in the greenhouse and multiple field environments. EpTFIIAγ physically interacts with endogenous transcriptional activators to synergistically enhance both stress-responsive and developmental transcriptional programs, simultaneously boosting photosynthetic capacity and water-use efficiency, while delaying senescence via multiple physiological and developmental enhancements, ultimately increasing grain yields. EpTFIIAγ uncouples antagonistic stress-response and biomass production pathways in multiple crops and delivers a straightforwards and broad-spectrum strategy for sustainably improving staple-crop yields regardless of water availability.

The bulk of crop production worldwide strictly depends on rainfall to support irrigation needs, and limitations on water availability pose a global challenge for agricultural productivity, with water scarcity and drought stress incurring unpredictable and potentially catastrophic effects on yield1,2. The adverse effects of climate change on crop productivity have historically been underestimated5. With the average global temperature expected to increase by 1.5–2.0 °C by 2050, the frequency and severity of drought events will be further increased, which could be accompanied by 30–40% reductions in food production3,4. Despite facing the greatest food-security challenges in the modern era7,8, annual crop yield improvement rates have not kept pace with projected food demands, that is, a 50–70% increase to accommodate approximately 9.8 billion people worldwide by 2050 (ref. 9), further compounding the effects of disaster events and decreasing availability of arable land.

According to recent reports, conventional plant-breeding efforts have boosted crop yields in water-limited environments, for example, through improved stress resistance, greater biomass accumulation, delayed leaf senescence or ‘stay-green’ strategies7,10, but broad potential remains for improving yield and yield stability across growing regions regardless of water availability11,12. Increasingly precise genetic modification strategies have advanced crop engineering for drought resistance13,14,15,16,17. For example, heterologous expression of a rice trehalose-6-phosphate phosphatase in developing maize ears improves yield under both well-watered and drought-stress conditions in the field16. In cassava, expressing a modified Arabidopsis potassium (K+) channel in vascular tissues improves K+ transport, photosynthesis and root biomass, allowing enhanced productivity in nutrient-poor and drought-prone environments17. However, genetic modification usually cannot provide a single, universal solution to multifactorial drought stress, and this approach frequently fails to improve yields in the field13,18 because drought resistance is a complex quantitative trait involving a multitude of small-effect loci or genes mediating diverse stress responses, such as stomatal closure (for reduced transpiration) or modified root architecture (for enhanced water uptake)10,19. Drought resistance typically accompanies trade-offs by way of reduced yield in the absence of stress6,20, undermining the effectiveness of certain genetic modification strategies. Therefore, of the genes identified in controlled conditions that often show limited effects in real-world environments, relatively few undergo rigorous field trials to properly demonstrate consistent agronomic value21.

According to recent reports, among known genetic resources for drought resistance, lichens have been generally overlooked despite their ubiquitous distribution across extreme ecological niches. In arid-adapted lichens, mycobionts appear to contribute more to survival under water deficit than photobionts22,23. We have previously isolated the lichen-forming fungus Endocarpon pusillum, which has extreme drought resistance. Exposure to dehydration stress identified 1,781 differentially expressed E. pusillum genes24. Through mining those data, here we identified the transcription factor gene EpTFIIAγ that broadly enhances yield and biomass production under field conditions when heterologously expressed in the world’s top-three-produced staple cereal crops of bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L.), maize (Zea mays L.) and rice (Oryza sativa L.). EpTFIIAγ delays plant senescence, enhances photosynthetic capacity, water-use efficiency (WUE) and drought resistance by functioning as a transcriptional co-factor to coordinately target multiple genes and pathways. EpTFIIAγ binds to TATA-box-containing motifs and interacts with several endogenous wheat transcriptional activators to synergistically enhance networks involved in stress responses, plant development, photosynthesis and grain yield. Our results provide an unprecedented broad-spectrum resource for crop improvement and highlight the untapped potential of lichen mycobionts as sources of versatile transgenes for biotechnology.

It has been revealed that among 25 differentially expressed genes predicted to encode transcription factors identified under dehydration stress in E. pusillum (Fig. 1a), EPUS02736 exhibits the strongest upregulation and encodes a transcription initiation factor IIA γ-chain (designated EpTFIIAγ). EpTFIIAγ shares homology with TFIIAs from plants, such as Arabidopsis, wheat, rice and maize, although the genetic relatedness between EpTFIIAγ and these homologues is relatively distant (Fig. 1b). Strong expression under dehydration stress implicates EpTFIIAγ in drought adaptation of the lichen mycobiont. Towards understanding its functionality, EpTFIIAγ was expressed in the yeast ∆hog1 mutant (deficient in HOG1, which encodes the high osmolarity glycerol 1 protein kinase), resulting in remarkably enhanced growth on solid synthetic dropout (SD) −Ura medium with 0.75 M sorbitol (Fig. 1c), and statistically significantly higher growth in corresponding liquid medium than the control (Fig. 1d). These results suggested that EpTFIIAγ contributes to regulating osmotic stress.

To determine whether EpTFIIAγ could also enhance drought resistance in plants, we first expressed endogenous TFIIAγ genes from Arabidopsis and wheat in the yeast hog1 mutant; however, no obvious effect on osmotic stress tolerance was observed (Fig. 1c), suggesting that TFIIAγ genes probably mediate divergent biological functions between plants and E. pusillum. We then generated three genetically independent transgenic Arabidopsis lines (TL1–TL3) constitutively and heterologously expressing EpTFIIAγ and examined drought resistance. To our surprise, seedlings expressing EpTFIIAγ had survival rates approximately seven times higher than wild-type Col-0 controls under drought-stress conditions (Fig. 1e). This improved drought resistance was not limited to the eudicot Arabidopsis. Transgenic wheat cv. Fielder seedlings heterologously expressing EpTFIIAγ from the strong and constitutive Ubiquitin promoter showed an approximately 3.5-fold increase in survival rate compared with wild-type Fielder under drought stress (Fig. 1f). However, overexpression of endogenous AtTFIIAγ or TaTFIIAγ in their respective native hosts had no such positive effect on drought resistance (Extended Data Fig. 1a–f), supporting their functional divergence from EpTFIIAγ. Analysis of key drought-resistance traits, including root architecture and biomass production (Extended Data Fig. 1g–o), stomatal density and aperture, and leaf water loss and transpiration (that is, leaf temperature; Extended Data Fig. 1p–u and Supplementary Fig. 1), suggested that the enhanced drought resistance among EpTFIIAγ transgenic Arabidopsis and wheat lines was mainly attributable to enhanced root growth and decreased stomatal aperture and transpiration compared with wild-type controls. Transgenic EpTFIIAγ wheat seedlings over-accumulated abscisic acid, auxin and salicylic acid hormones than wild-type Fielder plants under drought stress, whereas their accumulation remained comparable with that of controls under well-watered conditions (Supplementary Fig. 2).

It has been revealed that drought resistance varies widely across wheat germplasm25. To understand whether EpTFIIAγ can endow major commercially relevant wheat cultivars in China with enhanced drought resistance, we generated four genetically independent transgenic EpTFIIAγ lines in each of cvs. Xinong979 (XN979), Xinong511 (XN511), Jimai22 (JM22) and Xingzi9104 (XZ9104), which show different degrees of stress resistance and yield25,26. Greenhouse drought-resistance assays revealed that survival rates were 2–3 times higher for transgenic lines than corresponding wild-type controls (Fig. 1g–j), whereas stomatal aperture, leaf water loss rates and transpiration were also decreased in transgenic lines under drought stress (Supplementary Figs. 3 and 4). Therefore, heterologous EpTFIIAγ expression consistently endowed drought resistance and key physiological changes across four additional wheat cultivars. EpTFIIAγ plants also displayed broad-spectrum resilience to heat stress, lodging and multiple races of the major wheat stripe-rust fungal pathogen Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici (Extended Data Fig. 2), further supporting potential EpTFIIAγ deployment for engineering stacked resistance to environmental stressors in wheat.

Certain transgenes are known to improve resistance to drought stress but at the undesirable expense of reduced plant growth or productivity, known as yield drag13,18,20. We examined performance of all five sets of transgenic EpTFIIAγ wheat lines to identify potential yield drag in 3-year field trials under full-irrigation and water-limited conditions with a rain shelter in Yangling, China, which is characterized by a warm temperate semi-humid and semi-arid climate with 200–400 mm of rainfall during the growing season (Supplementary Fig. 5). All tested EpTFIIAγ lines had consistently increased grain yield across different genetic backgrounds and years compared with respective wild-type controls under full-irrigation control conditions. This increase was more pronounced under water-limited conditions (Fig. 1k–n; Supplementary Tables 1–3 and Supplementary Figs. 6–9). In 2025, grain yields surpassed that of the two previous years under water-limited conditions for EpTFIIAγ lines because of the higher temperature, lower rainfall and severe drought stress (Supplementary Fig. 5). Across all five backgrounds, EpTFIIAγ lines displayed 7.6–13.9% increases in grain yield per plant and 7.9–13.5% increases in yield per plot relative to controls under full-irrigation conditions, and increases of 22.3–38.3% in yield per plant and 19.4–32.8% higher yield per plot under water-limited conditions (Fig. 1m,n, Supplementary Tables 1–3 and Supplementary Fig. 7c,i). EpTFIIAγ lines were taller, had increased plant biomass, grain length, grain width and grain weight relative to respective wild-type controls, potentially contributing to increased plot yields. Despite higher grain yields, EpTFIIAγ plants had similar straw weight compared with wild-type plants, resulting in 6.1–14.8% higher harvest indices (that is, ratio of grain yield to aboveground biomass) under full irrigation and 7.6–15.5% increases in harvest indices under water-limited conditions (Supplementary Tables 1–3 and Supplementary Figs. 6 and 7). Growth duration was similar between genotypes under full irrigation, whereas time to maturity was 2–5 days longer for EpTFIIAγ transgenic lines than maturation time in the wild-type under water-limited conditions (Supplementary Fig. 7f,l), reflecting adaptation to drought stress.

Sources indicate that to evaluate trait stability, additional field trials were conducted in 2025 in three arid growing regions in China (Heyang, Shaanxi; Linfen, Shanxi; and Cangzhou, Hebei) with rainfall of 120–250 mm during the growing season. Grain yield per plant for EpTFIIAγ lines increased by 10.9–25.6% compared with wild-type controls, with the highest yield increases (15.6–25.6%) observed in Heyang (Supplementary Tables 4–6). These results underscored the potential of EpTFIIAγ as a valuable genetic resource for developing drought-resistant, high-yield wheat varieties in elite backgrounds regardless of water availability. In detail, EpTFIIAγ plants had expanded flag leaves, accelerated grain filling, larger pericarp cells, higher starch granule density and increased starch biosynthesis relative to wild-type controls under both full-irrigation and water-limited conditions (Extended Data Fig. 3 and Supplementary Fig. 10). This accelerated filling led to heavier grains beginning at 5 days after flowering, regardless of water conditions, resulting in 3.3–8.8% greater final grain weight in well-watered EpTFIIAγ plants and 15.2–21.4% higher grain weight in drought-stressed transgenic plants than in their respective wild-type controls (Fig. 1m,n, Supplementary Tables 1–3 and Supplementary Figs. 6 and 7). These improvements were consistent with the higher sucrose, glucose and fructose levels, as well as increased sucrose synthase, cell-wall invertase and ADP-glucose pyrophosphorylase activities observed in EpTFIIAγ grains during the early filling stage (Extended Data Fig. 4). Conversely, flag-leaf sheaths of EpTFIIAγ plants had lower levels of these sugars than wild-type controls. These results suggested that the extended duration and enhanced rate of grain filling may be key determinants of increased final grain weight and yield in EpTFIIAγ plants.

Given the drought resistance and yield boosts endowed by EpTFIIAγ in transgenic wheat lines, we examined which physiological processes are altered. EpTFIIAγ plants had delayed senescence compared with controls under water-limited conditions (Supplementary Figs. 8 and 9), which we hypothesized might be due to increased WUE. We also hypothesised that carbon assimilation might be altered given that increases in yield and biomass require enhanced carbon fixation. To examine possible differences in water status and carbon assimilation between wild-type Fielder and EpTFIIAγ plants, we first used plant multispectral imaging to estimate normalized difference vegetation index and normalized water index values at seedling stage in a growth chamber. Transgenic plants indeed had higher normalized difference vegetation index and lower normalized water index values than Fielder plants under both well-watered and drought-stress conditions (Supplementary Fig. 11). EpTFIIAγ seedling leaves had lower 13C fractionation than Fielder during the 18 days of drought treatment following water withdrawal (Fig. 2a), indicating enhanced WUE in these transgenic plants. These results are consistent with the lower water loss rate and transpiration for EpTFIIAγ plants under drought-stress conditions (Extended Data Fig. 1p–u).

Sources indicate that to further assess the effects of EpTFIIAγ expression on carbon assimilation, we measured quantum yield of photosystem II photochemistry (ΦPSII). Transgenic EpTFIIAγ seedlings had approximately 14.6% higher ΦPSII than Fielder control plants under well-watered conditions, and approximately 29.9% greater ΦPSII under drought stress (Extended Data Fig. 5a,b). These results suggested that EpTFIIAγ expression led to enhanced maintenance of PSII activity. EpTFIIAγ plants had improved light–response and CO2–response curves of net photosynthesis (Fig. 2b,c). In addition, the abundance of PSI, PSII, cytochrome b6/f and LHC proteins, as well as RuBisCO subunits were all increased in transgenic plants under well-watered or drought-stress conditions (Extended Data Fig. 5d). RuBisCO activity was increased in EpTFIIAγ plants (Extended Data Fig. 5c), which agreed with A–Ci curves showing higher maximum rates of RuBisCO carboxylation and electron transport (Extended Data Fig. 5e–h). Consistent with these increases, EpTFIIAγ leaves over-accumulated sucrose, glucose, starch and soluble sugars (Extended Data Fig. 5i), further demonstrating enhanced carbon assimilation in these plants. Of note, drought stress triggered a marked accumulation of root soluble sugars (for example, sucrose, glucose and fructose) in EpTFIIAγ plants compared with Fielder, whereas no such difference was observed under optimal conditions (Extended Data Fig. 5j), aligning with enhanced root growth under drought stress.

Recent findings suggest that we next evaluated how EpTFIIAγ contributes to lifting photosynthetic capacity in field-grown plants. Chlorophyll content (soil and plant analyser development, SPAD), maximum quantum yield of PSII photochemistry (Fv/Fm) and photosynthetic rate were all enhanced in EpTFIIAγ transgenic plants in all five wheat cultivars compared with their corresponding wild-type controls at all of the tillering, stem elongation, flowering and milk development stages under both full-irrigation and water-limited conditions (Fig. 2d–g and Supplementary Figs. 12–17). However, stomatal conductance and transpiration rate were lower in transgenic plants under water-limited conditions, although some EpTFIIAγ lines had slightly higher stomatal conductance under full-irrigation conditions. In agreement with these results, WUE (that is, the ratio of net photosynthetic rate to transpiration rate) was improved in EpTFIIAγ plants under water-limited conditions (Fig. 2d–g and Supplementary Figs. 14–17). Under full-irrigation field conditions, no obvious phenotypic changes in root development were seen between wild-type Fielder and transgenic plants. By contrast, all EpTFIIAγ lines had increased root length and biomass compared with Fielder under water-limited conditions (Fig. 2h–j), aligning with the stay-green phenotype observed in shoots (Supplementary Figs. 8 and 9). Together, field-grown EpTFIIAγ wheat lines have enhanced WUE, resulting in slower water consumption, delayed senescence under water-limited conditions, and consequently more extensive root development, thereby facilitating greater water uptake. These data also suggested that enhanced photosynthetic capacity and CO2 assimilation contributed to the increased biomass and grain yield observed in EpTFIIAγ wheat plants.

It has been revealed that eukaryotic transcription initiation by RNA polymerase II (Pol II) requires numerous general transcription factors and cofactors to nucleate at core promoter sites, which typically contain several DNA sequence elements (for example, TATA boxes), to form the pre-initiation complex27. Among them, the transcription initiation factor TFIIA is a general cofactor that acts as an anti-repressor or co-activator27,28. In multicellular eukaryotes, the TFIIA complex typically comprises α-subunit, β-subunit and γ-subunit, encoded by TFIIAαβ and TFIIAγ genes27,29. To characterize the function of EpTFIIAγ, we first examined TFIIAγ sequences across species. EpTFIIAγ retains a conserved protein architecture while also harbouring a unique, lineage-specific N-terminal extension (Supplementary Table 7 and Supplementary Fig. 18). To determine whether EpTFIIAγ participates in transcription initiation, we first examined its subcellular localization in wheat protoplasts. EpTFIIAγ–GFP mainly localized to the nucleus, whereas intact TaTFIIAγ–GFP and AtTFIIAγ–GFP fusions revealed both nuclear and cytoplasmic localization (Extended Data Fig. 6a,b). To investigate whether EpTFIIAγ could interact with endogenous TFIIAαβ to form the TFIIA holocomplex in plants, we conducted yeast two-hybrid, luciferase-complementation imaging and pulldown assays. These experiments consistently demonstrated that EpTFIIAγ fails to detectably interact with either wheat or Arabidopsis TFIIAαβ, whereas both TaTFIIAγ and AtTFIIAγ could interact with their corresponding TFIIAαβ proteins to form complete TFIIA complexes (Extended Data Fig. 6c–g). These results indicated that EpTFIIAγ does not appear to function as a transcription initiation factor in plants, or at least does so differently from these expression hosts.

The TFIIA recognition element (IIARE) located upstream of the TATA box enhances recruitment of TFIIA and other components to activate transcription at TATA-box promoter motifs27,29. We asked whether EpTFIIAγ could similarly bind to such recognition sites. Electrophoretic mobility shift assays (EMSAs) indicated that MBP–EpTFIIAγ could indeed directly bind to an IIARE-containing TATA box, whereas neither wheat TaTFIIAγ nor Arabidopsis AtTFIIAγ displayed detectable binding (Extended Data Fig. 6h,i). Although fungal and plant TFIIAγ proteins share conserved α-helical and β-sheet architectures, EpTFIIAγ uniquely harbours an N-terminal intrinsically disordered region (IDR; Fig. 3a). Hypothesizing that this region may confer specialized biological function, we generated an IDR deletion variant (EpTFIIAγ(ΔIDR)). This truncation did not bind to IIARE-containing TATA-box fragments, and likewise, its nuclear localization was impaired (Fig. 3b,c and Extended Data Fig. 6j). Conversely, fusing the EpTFIIAγ-derived IDR to TaTFIIAγ or AtTFIIAγ conferred binding to probes carrying an IIARE-containing TATA box (Fig. 3b and Extended Data Fig. 6j).

It has been revealed that to test whether this IDR could drive liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS), we expressed EpTFIIAγ–GFP in Nicotiana benthamiana leaf epidermal cells. Upon hyperosmotic stress, EpTFIIAγ maintained a homogeneous nuclear distribution and did not coalesce into condensates under either stress or non-stress conditions (Supplementary Fig. 19a). Moreover, His–EpTFIIAγ did not detectably form dynamic droplets in vitro, indicating that its relatively short IDR was insufficient to trigger LLPS (Supplementary Fig. 19b). Further evaluation of chromatin-binding dynamics through fluorescence recovery after photobleaching and fluorescence correlation spectroscopy showed that EpTFIIAγ(ΔIDR) exhibited markedly shallower bleach depth and accelerated recovery kinetics (Fig. 3c and Supplementary Fig. 19c–h), indicating attenuated chromatin association and higher mobility than full-length control. Stable-transgenic EpTFIIAγ(ΔIDR) expression in wheat cv. Fielder conferred no obvious improvement in drought resistance relative to wild-type (Extended Data Fig. 6k–m), indicating that the IDR is indeed indispensable for EpTFIIAγ function in the drought-stress response.

It has been revealed that to identify EpTFIIAγ-binding sites across the wheat genome, we performed chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by sequencing (ChIP–seq) with transgenic plants stably expressing EpTFIIAγ–HA in the cv. Fielder (Fig. 3d). Across two replicates, 17,131 putative EpTFIIAγ-binding sites were identified, 85% of which are in intergenic regions and 15% in genic regions, including gene bodies as well as the 3-kb upstream and 300-bp downstream flanking sequences presumed to harbour the promoter and transcriptional terminator, respectively (Fig. 3e). Analysis of 2,570 genic binding sites identified 1,347 annotated genes bound by EpTFIIAγ–HA (Fig. 3f and Supplementary Table 8), and the core motif within these binding regions was enriched with a TATA-containing element (Fig. 3g). Gene Ontology analysis found that these EpTFIIAγ–HA target genes were enriched in terms related to stress responses, such as ‘transcriptional regulation’, ‘response to water deprivation’, ‘response to osmotic stress’, ‘response to cold’, ‘regulation of stomatal movement’ and ‘transpiration’; hormone responses, such as ‘response to abscisic acid (ABA)’, ‘response to auxin’ and ‘response to brassinosteroid’, as well as ‘photosynthesis’ and ‘chlorophyll biosynthesis’ (Fig. 3h). Further EMSAs confirmed that EpTFIIAγ could bind to promoter regions of 387 wheat genes, underscoring its capacity to regulate diverse biological pathways in planta, such as those related to stress response, development, photosynthesis and yield formation (Extended Data Fig. 7a, Supplementary Table 9 and Supplementary Fig. 20).

In a recent development, to define the regulatory network involved in the effects of EpTFIIAγ on photosynthetic efficiency, WUE and the drought-stress response, we compared transcriptomes of 20-day-old wild-type Fielder and EpTFIIAγ transgenic seedlings. This identified 1,953 differentially expressed genes (DEGs; fold change of more than 2 or less than 0.5, P < 0.05) in transgenic plants relative to Fielder, including 1,405 upregulated and 548 downregulated DEGs (Extended Data Fig. 7b–g and Supplementary Table 10). By examining overlap between ChIP–seq and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) datasets, we identified 1,056 candidate target genes that are potentially bound and transcriptionally regulated by EpTFIIAγ, including 824 upregulated and 232 downregulated genes in EpTFIIAγ plants (Extended Data Fig. 8a,b). Among them, stress-response-related genes involved in ABA and drought responses revealed strong enrichment (Extended Data Fig. 8c), such as wheat homologues of Arabidopsis MYBR1 (ref. 30), FBH4 (ref. 31) and DREB1C32 (Supplementary Tables 9 and 10). Other genes known to function in plant development, source–sink partitioning and grain yield were also present among upregulated DEGs, including the CONSTANS-like gene TaCol-B5 (ref. 33), wheat homologues of rice OsCIN2 (ref. 34) and OsSWEET4 (ref. 35), and homologues of Arabidopsis VND7 (ref. 36) and SWEET12 (ref. 37). Among photosynthesis-related DEGs, we found TaYCF9 and TaCP47, which are homologues of Arabidopsis PsbZ38 and CP47 (ref. 39) encoding subunits of the PSII reaction centre. In addition, we identified TaCOG1, a homologue of the Arabidopsis Dof transcription factor COG1, that promotes biomass accumulation by enhancing photosynthetic capacity40. TaGAPC1, a redox-dependent regulator of energy metabolism that mediates stress responses in Arabidopsis41, was also upregulated (Supplementary Tables 9 and 10).

MBP–EpTFIIAγ could bind in vitro to approximately 30-bp promoter fragments containing TATA motifs from TaDREB1C, TaFBH4, TaMYBR1, TaVND7, TaCol-B5, TaCIN2, TaSWEET4, TaSWEET12, TaYCF9, TaCP47, TaCOG1 and TaGAPC1, and this interaction could be compromised by competition from unlabelled probes (Fig. 3i, Extended Data Fig. 8d and Supplementary Fig. 21a). ChIP–quantitative PCR (qPCR) indicated that these promoter fragments showed greater enrichment in EpTFIIAγ–HA genomic DNA precipitated by anti-haemagglutinin antibody than by the immunoglobulin G (IgG) control (Fig. 3j and Extended Data Fig. 8e), demonstrating that EpTFIIAγ could indeed bind to TATA-containing core promoter motifs. In dual-luciferase reporter assays using approximately 1.5-kb promoter fragments, activities of target promoters were upregulated in the presence of EpTFIIAγ compared with empty vector controls (Fig. 3k, Extended Data Fig. 8f and Supplementary Fig. 21b), supported by real-time (RT)–qPCR analyses revealing that TaDREB1C, TaFBH4, TaMYBR1, TaVND7, TaCol-B5, TaCIN2, TaSWEET4, TaSWEET12, TaYCF9, TaCP47, TaCOG1 and TaGAPC1 mRNAs were all expressed at higher levels in all three EpTFIIAγ transgenic lines than in wild-type Fielder (Extended Data Fig. 8g). These results collectively indicated that EpTFIIAγ functions as a transcriptional cofactor to regulate target gene expression.

To determine how downstream regulatory targets contribute to enhancing drought resistance, photosynthetic efficiency and grain yield in EpTFIIAγ plants, we generated transgenic wheat lines overexpressing TaDREB1C, TaCOG1 or TaCIN2 in the cv. Fielder background. TaDREB1C lines had enhanced drought resistance and WUE through accelerated stomatal closure and reduced transpiration compared with Fielder under drought stress (Extended Data Fig. 9a–g). This overexpression did not detectably alter growth period, which remained comparable with controls under full irrigation (Extended Data Fig. 9h–j). Plants overexpressing TaCOG1 had enhanced photosynthetic and carbon-fixation capacities, resulting in increased biomass and grain yield relative to controls (Extended Data Fig. 9k–p). Moreover, TaCIN2 overexpression resulted in accelerated grain filling, ultimately increasing grain size and yield (Extended Data Fig. 9q–v). These results position the EpTFIIAγ regulon as pivotal for concurrently improving drought resilience and yield potential in wheat.

To investigate the mechanisms through which EpTFIIAγ drives enhanced drought resistance, photosynthetic capacity and grain yield, we conducted yeast two-hybrid screening using a cDNA library obtained from wheat cv. Chinese Spring seedlings. Four successive rounds of screening with EpTFIIAγ serving as bait yielded 112 candidate interacting proteins (Supplementary Table 11), including 22 putative transcription factors. After repeating yeast two-hybrid assays to confirm that EpTFIIAγ could interact with wheat homologues of Arabidopsis transcriptional activators WRKY46 (ref. 42), AKS1 (ref. 43), ARF6 (ref. 44) and VOZ1 (ref. 45) (Fig. 4a), luciferase-complementation imaging tested whether EpTFIIAγ could physically interact with these partners. Co-expression of EpTFIIAγ–C-terminal luciferase fragment (cLUC) with N-terminal luciferase fragment (nLUC)–TaWRKY46, nLUC–TaAKS1, nLUC–TaARF6 or nLUC–TaVOZ1 produced chemiluminescence, whereas no signal was observed in regions infiltrated with vector controls (Fig. 4b). Bimolecular fluorescence complementation assays further revealed that co-expression of the EpTFIIAγ–cYFP with nYFP–TaWRKY46, nYFP–TaAKS1, nYFP–TaARF6 or nYFP–TaVOZ1 led to obvious YFP signal (Fig. 4c and Supplementary Fig. 22a,b). Pulldown assays indicated that MBP–EpTFIIAγ could interact with GST–TaWRKY46, GST–TaAKS1, GST–TaARF6 and HA–TaVOZ1 in vitro (Fig. 4d). Co-immunoprecipitation assays in N. benthamiana leaves co-expressing 35Spro:GFP–EpTFIIAγ and 35Spro:mCherry–TaWRKY46, 35Spro:mCherry–TaARF6 or 35Spro:mCherry–EpTFIIAγ with 35Spro:GFP–TaAKS1, 35Spro:GFP–TaVOZ1 also confirmed that EpTFIIAγ could physically interact with these transcription factors in planta (Fig. 4e). By contrast, the IDR-deleted EpTFIIAγ variant failed to detectably interact with any tested partners (Supplementary Fig. 22c,d), highlighting the essential role of this IDR. Moreover, no interactions were observed between wheat TaTFIIAγ and the transcription factors TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 or TaVOZ1 (Supplementary Fig. 22e,f), underscoring EpTFIIAγ functional specificity.

Industry observers note that to map genome-wide binding sites and target genes, we used CUT&Tag in stable-transgenic cv. Fielder plants expressing TaWRKY46–HA, TaAKS1–FLAG, TaARF6–HA or TaVOZ1–HA. Integrative analysis identified 467, 309, 495 and 505 target genes that are potentially co-bound and co-regulated by EpTFIIAγ with TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 or TaVOZ1, respectively (Supplementary Table 12 and Supplementary Fig. 23), suggesting direct involvement in the EpTFIIAγ regulatory network. GST–TaWRKY46 could bind in vitro to probes containing the W-box from the TaCol-B5, TaSWEET4 and TaSWEET12 promoters, and these binding events increased in the presence of MBP–EpTFIIAγ (Fig. 4f and Extended Data Fig. 10a). Similarly, GST–TaAKS1 could bind to probes harbouring the G-box or E-box from the TaDREB1C, TaCol-B5, TaYCF9 or TaCOG1 promoter regions, with the addition of MBP–EpTFIIAγ markedly strengthening these interactions in vitro. Moreover, GST–TaARF6 could interact with AuxRE-containing probes derived from the TaYCF9, TaFBH4 and TaCIN2 promoters, which was boosted by addition of MBP–EpTFIIAγ, whereas GST–TaVOZ1 bound to probes with a 5′-CTTCTT-3′ motif present in the TaCP47, TaVND7, TaMYBR1 and TaGAPC1 promoter regions, which also increased in the presence of MBP–EpTFIIAγ (Fig. 4f and Extended Data Fig. 10a). Dual-luciferase reporter assays indicated that TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 and TaVOZ1 could activate genes with corresponding promoter recognition sites (Fig. 4g and Extended Data Fig. 10b).

In a recent development, to determine whether EpTFIIAγ functions coordinately with or independently of TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 and TaVOZ1 in regulating target genes, we performed dual-luciferase reporter assays. Upon co-expressing EpTFIIAγ with each respective transcription factor, LUC activity driven by the TaDREB1C, TaFBH4, TaMYBR1, TaVND7, TaCol-B5, TaCIN2, TaSWEET4, TaSWEET12, TaYCF9, TaCP47, TaCOG1 and TaGAPC1 promoters was greater than the expression of wheat transcription factors alone (Fig. 4g and Extended Data Fig. 10b). To clarify whether activation of these transcription-factor genes contributed to the observed drought resistance of transgenic EpTFIIAγ plants, we examined drought resistance in lines overexpressing TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 and TaVOZ1 (Extended Data Fig. 11a–d), as well as wrky46-knockout and arf6-knockout mutants by gene editing in cv. Fielder (Extended Data Fig. 11e,f). All overexpression lines had enhanced drought resistance relative to Fielder, whereas both mutants had compromised drought resistance compared with Fielder controls (Extended Data Fig. 11g–j). To further characterize the genetic interactions of EpTFIIAγ with TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 and TaVOZ1, we crossed EpTFIIAγ plants (Fielder background) with each overexpression line. Under normal conditions, homozygous double-transgene-positive progeny of all crosses bore phenotypes comparable with that of TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 and TaVOZ1 overexpression plants. By contrast, double-transgene-carrying hybrids demonstrated stronger drought resistance than control plants expressing a single transgene (Extended Data Fig. 11k,l). These findings collectively demonstrated that EpTFIIAγ physically interacts with select transcription activators, such as TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 or TaVOZ1, and that their interactions resulted in additive effects on EpTFIIAγ target gene expression, consequently enhancing the drought response, photosynthesis and grain yield.

According to recent reports, to determine whether EpTFIIAγ function in conferring drought resistance was conserved in other major cereal crops, we generated three transgenic EpTFIIAγ lines each in rice cv. Nipponbare and maize inbred line B73 backgrounds (Fig. 5a,b). In greenhouse drought-resistance assays, survival of transgenic EpTFIIAγ rice and maize lines was extended by approximately 2.6-fold and approximately 2.8-fold for rice (Fig. 5c,d) and maize (Fig. 5e,f), respectively, compared with their wild-type controls. Transcriptomic analysis found that genes involved in ‘transcriptional regulation’, ‘response to ABA’, ‘response to water deprivation’, ‘response to osmotic stress’ and ‘photosynthesis’ were enriched among upregulated DEGs in EpTFIIAγ seedlings of both species (Extended Data Fig. 12a,b and Supplementary Tables 13 and 14).
