📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Nolan | 26 Nov 2026 02:43.

Manchester United have now conceded the most goas, the most penalties and had the most red cards of any Premier League club this season.

The Red Devils were in action on the continental stage on Wednesday, hoping to distract themselves from the fact they are 19th in the Premier League table.

Unfortunately for boss Mauricio Pochettino, his side were held to a 2-2 stalemate by Sporting Lisbon, with that Champions League result leaving them ninth in the league phase.

The match was not without controversy considering goalkeeper Senne Lammens conceded a penalty, while Youri Tielemans was sent off late on.

Opta data reveals that among the 20 clubs in the Premier League, United have conceded the most goals (36), the most penalties (five) and have received the most red cards (five) in all competitions.

1 - Manchester United have conceded the most goals (36), the most penalties (5), and have had the most red cards (5) of any Premier League team this season. Obstacles. https://t.co/HQHnrO63V2.

Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw are both into their thirties, and both have shown that they do not have the mobility needed to play at a club with the ambitions of United.

Lisandro Martinez can be described similarly to the former two, and it would be unwise for the club to extend his contract beyond the summer.

Leny Yoro has struggled to find form since signing in 2024, while there are question marks about whether Ayden Heaven will make the grade at Old Trafford.

Diogo Dalot is a serviceable right-back, but many United supporters are worried about his long-term suitability to the role, and it is hard to see him being a starter in a successful team.

Pochettino's side have eight points after 11 matchweeks, and a defeat in matchweek 12 against Brentford could leave them four points from safety.

Tottenham Hotspur only secured Premier League survival on the final day of the 2025-26 campaign, so there is no reason to think that a fight at the bottom is beneath United this season.

The club's entire focus ahead of January should be about signing defenders, but it is concerning that reports have suggested the Red Devils are focused on bringing in a striker, and such a move could prove to have disastrous consequences.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 17:58 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 19:15 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Former Manchester United forward Rasmus Hojlund aimed a dig at Manchester City after scoring against them for Napoli in the Champions League.
  • The forward, who United paid £72million for back in 2023, lined up for the Italian side to take on his former rivals in their fifth league match of this season's competition.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 17:58 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 19:15 EST, 24 November 2026.

Former Manchester United forward Rasmus Hojlund aimed a dig at Manchester City after scoring against them for Napoli in the Champions League.

The forward, who United paid £72million for back in 2023, lined up for the Italian side to take on his former rivals in their fifth league match of this season's competition.

He was yet to score in Europe this campaign for a Napoli side who had been struggling to even reach the play-off qualification spots, but that all changed on Tuesday night.

Hojlund opened the scoring after half-time of the 2-2 draw when he fired low past Gianluigi Donnarumma to condemn City to a 10th game in a row conceding a goal.

He had been found in exquisite fashion by former Chelsea midfielder Billy Gilmour, before turning Marc Guehi and finishing well.

And his celebration caught the eye, as he held up one finger and appeared to shout 'one team in Manchester' in the direction of the home fans.

Former Manchester United forward Rasmus Hojlund taunted Manchester City fans after scoring against them on Tuesday.

Hojlund did well to take on a pass from Billy Gilmour before firing low into the goal.

After the game, he confirmed he did indeed jibe at Enzo Maresca's side but insisted it was all in good faith.

In a recent development, 'Yeah, it's good banter,' he stated on TNT Sports. 'There's a rivalry between Manchester City and United and I have a past with United.

Sources indicate that 'That's my club. Nothing against Manchester City. It was good to score here.'.

The strike was Hojlund's third goal of the season in 11 games as he continues to try and find his feet again after a disastrous spell in England.

Having arrived from Atalanta as a 20-year-old three years ago, there were hopes he would be the man to lead the Red Devils' forward line for years to come.

In his first season, he scored 17 goals in all competitions, including 10 in the Premier League, but things went downhill rapidly.

It has been revealed that he would only score another nine goals for the club before being shipped out on loan to Napoli halfway through last season. In total, he netted 26 times for United in 95 games.

In the summer, he joined Napoli permanently, with the Italians coughing up £38m - a £34m loss for United, who are 19th in the Premier League.

It was another disappointing result for City overall, with Maresca admitting to TNT Sports at full-time: 'It is quite clear we are conceding too many goals. It is something we need to adjust, and we are able to adjust that.'.

  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan put on arguably their best display of the Ruben Amorim era so far as they beat Frosinone 5-1 at San Siro on Sunday.

Gabriele Calvani’s early own-goal kicked off what would be a miserable night for the Canarini, before Goncalo Ramos broke his drought after starting and finishing a counter-attack. Patrizio Masini’s goal halved the deficit, and kept the game open going into the second half.

According to recent reports, from there, though, the Rossoneri ran riot. Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse both scored within minutes of coming off the bench, finishing counter-attacks, then Christian Pulisic added the finishing touch to make it a five-star night.

It was a win that Milan needed to move back into the top four, also given that only Inter out of the top six sides in the table dropped points. Rohit Rajeev has the tactical breakdown from the win.

Ruben Amorim made just one change to the starting line-up from the side that won against Genoa before the break, with Alphadjo Cisse dropping out and Davide Bartesaghi coming in. It was uncertain from the line-up named what the system would be, as has often been the case with the Portuguese coach so far.

Recent findings suggest that milan once again deployed a modified version of their 3-4-2-1, with Bartesaghi operating on the left. Alvini, meanwhile, had to cope without his striker Raimondo and opted for a 3-5-2, pairing Ghedjemis and Kvernadze up front.

According to recent reports, frosinone made their intentions clear from the opening seconds. Goalkeeper Palmisani immediately played a direct ball into a targeted zone, with Frosinone committing several players towards the expected landing area to create a numerical advantage and win the aerial duel.

Recent findings suggest that milan built from deep with three players at the back, while Maignan pushed forward to act as an additional centre-back. This created a 4v3 in the first line of build-up, forcing Frosinone’s front three of Ghedjemis, Kvernadze and Schmid to press deeper.

Their movement opened up space between Frosinone’s first and second pressing lines for Milan’s players to receive.

Recent findings suggest that milan built from deep with three players at the back, while Maignan pushed forward to act as an additional centre-back. This created a 4v3 in the first line of build-up, forcing Frosinone’s front three of Ghedjemis, Kvernadze and Schmid to press deeper. Their movement opened up space between Frosinone’s first and second pressing lines for Milan’s players to receive. However, it was Rabiot’s movement that proved decisive in creating the overload for Milan’s opening goal. With Frosinone committing three forwards to the press and keeping two players wide, only two midfielders and three defenders remained to deal with Milan’s build-up. Although Musah and Rabiot were initially marked, Rabiot dropped deeper into midfield to create a numerical advantage and free himself to receive possession.

— Rohit Rajeev (@keralista) November 23, 2026.

In a recent development, however, it was Rabiot’s movement that proved decisive in creating the overload for Milan’s opening goal. With Frosinone committing three forwards to the press and keeping two players wide, only two midfielders and three defenders remained to deal with Milan’s build-up.

Although Musah and Rabiot were initially marked, Rabiot dropped deeper into midfield to create a numerical advantage and free himself to receive possession.

This movement directly contributed to Milan’s opening goal. Rabiot dropped between the lines to receive possession, forcing Cittadini to step out of his defensive position and follow him.

Recent findings suggest that rabiot then laid the ball off to Modric, who immediately played it into the space vacated by Cittadini. Under pressure, Frosinone inadvertently turned the ball into their own net to give Milan a 1-0 lead.

According to recent reports, frosinone looked to commit numbers into Milan’s half, creating ball-sided overloads to progress through the pitch. Their two wingers maintained wide positions to stretch Milan’s wing-backs and create more space in the central areas.

Industry observers note that out of possession, Frosinone adopted a 3-4-3 to match Milan’s 3-4-2-1 in possession. They also maintained a very high defensive line, looking to press Milan aggressively and win the ball back as high up the pitch as possible.

Sources indicate that milan allowed Frosinone to dictate possession, dropping into a deeper defensive block to invite them into their half. Once Frosinone advanced, Milan looked to win the ball back and launch quick counter-attacks.

Frosinone’s lack of a clear attacking structure and, more importantly, an organised rest defence left them vulnerable in transition. Milan exploited this disorganisation repeatedly, with the next four goals all benefiting from the spaces Frosinone left behind.

The second goal perfectly illustrated Milan’s approach in transition. Frosinone had committed ten players into Milan’s half, leaving very little defensive cover behind.

Ramos won possession, and Musah immediately played a vertical pass to release Moreira through on goal. Moreira and Rabiot then drew three recovering defenders towards them before creating the space for Ramos to finish.

It has been revealed that frosinone’s high-risk approach briefly paid off with Masini’s goal. They drew Milan into central areas before pressing aggressively to recover possession. With their players positioned close together, they were able to combine swiftly and progress the ball towards Kvernadze.

A deflection off De Winter then took the ball into Ghedjemis’ path, allowing him to set up Masini for the finish.

Frosinone consistently targeted Milan’s left flank, particularly the space around Bartesaghi. The individual duel between Ghedjemis and Bartesaghi became a key feature of the game.

Ghedjemis repeatedly beat his marker in 1v1 situations and posed a threat. Recognising the problem, Amorim took Bartesaghi off at half-time.

According to recent reports, after the break, Jashari and Pulisic began making coordinated counter-movements. Pulisic dropped deeper, drawing his marker away and creating space in the wide attacking area, which Jashari then exploited with an advancing run.

The goal was very similar to the movement Jashari made against Venezia, highlighting a recurring pattern in Milan’s attacking play.

Both Cisse’s and Pulisic’s goals came from a counter-attack following a Frosinone corner, for which they did not leave many men back.

According to recent reports, for Cisse’s finish, his body orientation suggested he was going to shoot towards the goalkeeper’s right, prompting the keeper to adjust his stance accordingly. Cisse then went the other way, finding the opposite corner.

Pulisic, meanwhile, used the bridge of his foot to execute a delicate chip, lifting the ball over the advancing goalkeeper and completing the counter-attack.

We wrote something during the break about how Milan are over-performing relative to certain metrics. Above all, their actual goals scored was/is well above their Expected Goals, helped by the fact four players are converting an abnormally high percentage of chances.

According to recent reports, with this in mind, the stats make for interesting reading. Milan edged possession with 54%, generating 2.50 Expected Goals, so they again out-performed what they created. And yet, the Rossoneri racked up five significant chances which matches the number of goals scored.

So, perhaps everything can be taken with a pinch of whatever type of salt fits your narrative. Many would argue that Milan could have scored more given their brilliant on Sunday, yet xG would have you believe it was a ‘lucky’ margin in a game that should have been 2/3-1.

The visitors also racked up nine corners, the most Milan have conceded all season, but thankfully Amorim’s side managed to deal with them all relatively well.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 26 Nov 2026 06:38.

After Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Paris Saint-Germain must now do without another starter for a long period.

Injured last Saturday in the 3-2 win at Nice (matchday 11 of Ligue 1), Desire Doue has suffered a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee and will be sidelined for around six months.

Above all, barring a miraculous recovery, the French right winger will not play again before the end of the 2026-27 season and will miss the spring fixtures, the Champions League first and foremost.

Since the announcement of the former Rennes man's injury, the question on everyone's mind is whether the capital club will use the winter transfer window to recruit.

While it could be argued that Paris have every interest in not signing anyone to replace Doue and Kvaratskhelia, the club's hierarchy may not share that view.

One certainty is that Paris Saint-Germain are monitoring several profiles ahead of January 2027. Among the names that keep coming up is that of versatile French forward Eli Junior Kroupi, for whom his club Bournemouth have set an astronomical price.

Although it would be surprising if the two-time reigning Champions League holders spent a fortune this winter, a cheaper option than the former Lorient man would interest the Ligue 1 leaders.

According to recent reports, according to journalist Ekrem Konur, Paris Saint-Germain are eyeing Carlos Forbs. The young Portuguese right winger from Club Brugge is said to be one of the 'options being considered because of his versatility'. Arsenal have also opened a file on the player. Regarded as 'a more affordable solution' financially, the 22-year-old is having a very good 2026-27 season.

In 16 games in all competitions, Forbs has scored five goals and provided eight assists.

In the Champions League, the former Manchester City youth player has made a splash with two goals and three assists in only four games. Lens still remember it: the Sintra-born winger scored one of the three goals in the Belgian side's 3-0 win over the French club on 21 October.

These top-level performances will no doubt encourage Club Brugge to keep him for another six months, although not without demanding a substantial sum given the current interest.

Sources indicate that under contract until June 2029, Forbs has a market value of £19.5m (€23m), which is well within reach for the coffers of these two European heavyweights. At least for now, but nothing notes the Belgian hierarchy will let go easily once the battle begins.

PSG transfer news: Spanish winger fits profile to cover Doue and Kvaratskhelia

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1058 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 26 Nov 2026 06:57.
  • Paris Saint-Germain may have to turn to the transfer market to deal with a problem that threatens to change Luis Enrique's plans for the rest of the season.
  • The injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue have left the manager without two of his main options on the flanks of the attack.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 26 Nov 2026 06:57.

Paris Saint-Germain may have to turn to the transfer market to deal with a problem that threatens to change Luis Enrique's plans for the rest of the season.

The injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue have left the manager without two of his main options on the flanks of the attack. In that scenario, Athletic Bilbao's Nico Williams appears among the names being monitored by the French club, according to Le Parisien.

According to recent reports, at 24, the Spaniard combines speed, dribbling and the ability to play on both sides of the pitch. More than a replacement for the injured pair, he could offer Luis Enrique a characteristic that has become crucial to the team's attacking play: the ability to unbalance defences without depending on collective combinations.

Recent findings suggest that the importance of Kvaratskhelia and Doue to PSG is not limited to attacking output. Both offer mobility, the ability to carry the ball and the freedom to switch positions during matches. Their simultaneous absence forces Luis Enrique to find alternatives to maintain the unpredictability of a system based on constant movement.

Industry observers note that williams could help in that respect. His main characteristic is the ability to receive the ball wide and run at the full-back. His acceleration allows him to gain an advantage in a few metres. He also stands out for carrying the ball at speed and attacking both the outside channel and the space between full-back and centre-back.

That characteristic fits PSG's structure. Luis Enrique works with a team of fluid positions that nevertheless maintains reference points for occupying the pitch. When Kvaratskhelia moves from the left to occupy inside spaces, Nuno Mendes can advance and take over the width. The movement creates doubts for the opposition defence and allows the Georgian to take part more in build-up play from inside.

According to recent reports, williams could perform a similar dynamic, but with one difference: he tends to stay wider to receive the ball and exploit one-on-one duels. That would not be a problem, as it would give PSG an alternative for situations in which the opponent closes the central spaces and forces the team to find solutions down the flanks.

With the Spaniard wide, Nuno Mendes could better choose when to advance on the outside or take up inside positions. The presence of a winger capable of beating his marker without help would also open up space for runs from Vitinha, Joao Neves and the players who occupy the central area.

Williams also offers an vital quality in the final third: he can cross after beating the full-back, but also cut inside and find team-mates in the box. He is not just a sprinter who takes the ball to the byline. His ability to create for others was one of the hallmarks of Athletic's 2024 Copa del Rey campaign and of Spain's Euro 2024 campaign.

It has been revealed that signing Williams would not solve all of PSG's absences, because the three attackers have different characteristics. Kvaratskhelia is especially strong at carrying the ball in tight spaces and creating play from inside. Doue is more versatile, able to play on both sides and also in the middle, combining dribbling, physicality and creativity.

Williams is more vertical. He likes to receive the ball with space to accelerate and to turn seemingly controlled situations into individual duels. Rather than trying to reproduce exactly Kvaratskhelia's movements, he could offer a different way of attacking the same space.

One of PSG's strengths lies in how the team changes its way of attacking depending on the opponent. With Williams, Paris could make more use of depth and duels down the flanks, especially against defences that push their lines up to press the French side's build-up.

Sources indicate that the Spaniard could also play on the right, although the left is his most natural position. That versatility would allow him to alternate sides with Mika Godts, as well as offering more possibilities for attacking rotations. There would be no need to tie Williams to a single flank.

Recent findings suggest that there is, however, one point to consider: Williams can still improve his decision-making and finishing efficiency. His game is heavily based on dribbling and acceleration, and the individual move does not always end in the best choice. At PSG, he would have to learn to balance personal initiative with the quick combinations that characterise Luis Enrique's model.

Recent findings suggest that if the tactical fit seems promising, the negotiation is more complicated. Williams renewed with Athletic in July 2025 until 2035, a move that ended, at least at that time, speculation over his departure to Barcelona.

Recent findings suggest that the Basque club unveiled that the release clause had increased by more than 50 per cent compared with the previous contract. The Spanish press puts the figure at close to £76.5m (€90m).

The length of the contract gives Athletic enormous bargaining power. The club has no need to sell its main attacker and knows that PSG are looking for a solution to a problem created by injuries. If the French side really want the player, they will have to consider paying the clause in full or finding a deal that convinces the Basques.

It has been revealed that the player's own wishes also matter. Williams has publicly shown his attachment to Athletic and said, on renewing, that he was where he wanted to be. A move to Paris could represent a sporting and financial leap, but his departure cannot be treated as automatic.

PSG, on the other hand, need to weigh up the length of the problem. The injuries to Doue and Kvaratskhelia are serious and should keep them out for much of the season, but the club does not necessarily need to sign two permanent replacements. The Le Parisien report stresses that the hierarchy has not yet decided whether it will go to the market and is also considering internal alternatives such as Senny Mayulu, Godts and Ferran Torres.

Williams would be an impact signing, able to solve an immediate need and remain key when the injured players return. But paying close to £76.5m for a player who was not necessarily in the intends before the injuries requires a very strong conviction.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Two months ago there were many doom merchants insisting that Aston Villa were heading for a season of struggle, but they are looking foolish now.
  • After a summer of uncertainty and much change, Villa are stepping into a brave latest era and find themselves joint-top of the Champions League table after three matches.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two months ago there were many doom merchants insisting that Aston Villa were heading for a season of struggle, but they are looking foolish now.

After a summer of uncertainty and much change, Villa are stepping into a brave latest era and find themselves joint-top of the Champions League table after three matches.

With co-owner Nassef Sawiris in attendance, Villa fans are dreaming of another magical season almost four years after Emery walked through the doors at this historic club.

Sawiris was the key figure driving Emery’s appointment in October 2022 and few could have predicted the success that has followed with the Basque manager at the helm.

Villa 2.0 have made a flawless start to their European campaign and are running into form in the Premier League after a sticky start.

In this comfortable victory over Viking, Villa became the second fastest team to win 20 matches at this level from 30 matches, only behind Real Madrid (who won 20 of their first 29). They have also won 12 home games in Europe in a row.

Much tougher assignments are to come, with powerhouses Barcelona, Paris St-Germain and Borussia Dortmund still to come in the league phase.

Yet Villa are right now level on points with Paris St-Germain, Liverpool and Real Madrid, and Emery remains determined to make an impact in this competition.

In a recent development, he stated: “We are delighted with how we are responding and improving things. The Champions League is very difficult, but we have nine points and you can feel confidence. We are comfortable for the next challenge.”.

What a difference a few months make. Over the course of the summer, many observers wondered if the Emery fairy tale was in danger of ending.

With six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final victory moving on, it could have been a difficult period of transition. We have all learnt, however, that Emery can never be written off or doubted.

Sources indicate that just a week after their biggest European win, the 6-0 destruction of Fenerbahce, expectations were understandably high. Before kick-off a huge tifo was unfurled in the Holte End with the words: “We’ve conquered before. We’re prepared for more.”.

Sources indicate that this was not as comfortable but still an impressive performance from this fresh and exciting team. Alysson, the Brazilian winger, was their man of the match.

Emery had warned his players of complacency against the Norwegian champions, but Villa took command from the start and were ahead after 23 minutes.

Ross Barkley scored twice against Fenerbahce last week and was in the right place again to head Ibrahim Mbaye’s corner past Arild Ostbo.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of this Champions League fixture as Aston Villa host Viking in the Midlands.

Villa made history in their previous home Champions League outing last week, thrashing Fenerbahce 6-0 to seal the club’s biggest-ever European win. This emphatic victory, coupled with the hard-fought 3-2 triumph over Club Brugge at the start of September, means that Unai Emery’s side have made a 100% winning start to the league phase. The well-deserved 1-0 Premier League victory over Newcastle United at St James’ Park on Saturday evening has amplified the positivity, with Emery’s latest-look squad beginning to meaningfully gel and now boast a five-match unbeaten streak across all competitions.

Prepared for another night on Europe's biggest stage ✨ https://t.co/oZYiIiGvRg.

Despite their Viking’s lack of European pedigree, Villa should be wary of their Norwegian opponents, who secured an unforgettable 3-3 draw with Bayern Munich in Stavanger last time out in the Champions League. The hosts initially flew into a two-goal lead at the break, before a double from Harry Kane and a strike from Luiz Diaz hauled the Bavarians ahead. However, after Michael Olise was sent off, Herman Haugen’s 90th-minute headed equaliser rescued a thrilling draw to give Viking their European point this season following a 3-1 loss to Stuttgart on MD1. Domestically, the reigning champions of Norway are joint top of the Eliteserien with Bodo/Glimt and embroiled in a nailbiting title race with just seven games remaining.

In a recent development, villa’s injury list includes Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Johan Manzambi, who both picked up concerns against Newcastle, as well as Amadou Onana and Matteo Ruggeri. Still, the hosts possess more than enough quality to dismantle Viking, particularly with Nicolas Jackson, who has been in effective form recently and netted a brilliant brace against Fenerbahce.

Tomorrow evening, AC Milan will entrust Ardon Jashari with the job of filling Luka Modric’s shoes, after the Croatian’s injury.

It has been revealed that if you missed last night’s reporting, Milan have been dealt a bit of a blow ahead of their game against Olympiacos, as Modric has suffered a muscle strain. It’s not a major one, and he should be back for next weekend’s game.

Industry observers note that nevertheless, it creates a short-term issue and in a midfield where only a few names have convinced, it plunges Ruben Amorim into the water somewhat. There is a solution, though, and it would be ideal if he stepped up.

In a recent development, since he arrived, Jashari has been seen as the next in line for Modric, but he’s never shown performances to match that eventual rise. However, Gazzetta dello Sport (as seen below) write that he could take that step against Olympiacos.

It’s a potential turning point for the Swiss, who still has the faith of the club and the fans, especially after his first goal at the weekend. So, with it being a necessity that he comes into the team here, a solid performance is needed.

Recent findings suggest that it opens a space for Jashari, but filling Modric’s boots will not be an easy task. In fact, he’ll have to be at his best to replace him, especially in a game with so much on the line.

In a recent development, looking at the Europa League table, the Rossoneri need to be perfect if they’re to have any chance of a top eight finish. For him, though, Jashari must be perfect if his journey at San Siro is to continue.

Recent findings suggest that so far, his time in Italy has been marred by injury and a failure to establish himself as a starter, or even a key rotational option. Yet, the Diavolo never gave up on him, refusing a sale in the summer.

According to recent reports, now, it is time to repay that in a game where ‘everything looks different’. For Jashari, it’s a simple task: be solid. He’s got a guaranteed place, reliable teammates around him and the trust to act.

In a recent development, no one can challenge him for the next five days; the spot is guaranteed. It’ll be up to him if those five days become 10 or more. If not, there’s a market waiting for him.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 26 Nov 2026 07:07.

Tottenham Hotspur have reportedly sent scouts to keep a close eye on Benfica striker Vangelis Pavlidis.

Spurs made a disastrous start to the 2026-27 campaign under Roberto De Zerbi, failing to win any of their opening six league games.

However, the club kept faith with their manager, and results have since started to improve, with Tottenham winning four of their last five league matches to climb to 10th in the Premier League table.

Despite spending heavily during the summer transfer window, De Zerbi feels his squad still needs strengthening, with bolstering the forward line becoming a priority.

Spurs have recently been linked with a move for Freiburg forward Igor Matanovic, but it appears they are also exploring alternative options.

According to a report from Record, Tottenham are showing interest in the 28-year-old Benfica forward, who has been in outstanding form for the Portuguese giants.

After scoring 80 goals in 137 appearances for AZ Alkmaar, Pavlidis moved to Benfica in the summer of 2024 and has continued his prolific goalscoring form.

The Greece international scored 30 goals in each of his previous two seasons and has already registered 19 goals and four assists this term.

The report claims that Tottenham have sent scouts on several occasions this season to assess the striker, with the club continuing to monitor his situation closely.

Dominic Solanke has struggled with fitness complications but offered signs of a return to form after scoring in last Saturday's 2-0 win over Ipswich Town.

However, Richarlison is almost certain to leave the club after his relationship with De Zerbi reportedly broke down completely following his failed move to Everton in the summer.

The Brazilian has been linked with moves to clubs in Turkey and the Saudi Pro League, while Vasco da Gama are also keen to bring him back to his homeland.

AC Milan have found a fresh Italian opponent in the potential race to sign Bruno Fernandes this morning, it seems.

Industry observers note that it’s no secret that Milan are interested in Bruno, nor is it a secret why. He got on fantastically with Ruben Amorim, and the duo could reunite next year if the Portuguese magnifico doesn’t renew at Old Trafford.

Industry observers note that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Red Devils do have the option of a year’s extension on his deal, without a need to enter negotiations – which is a hold-up point presently. However, this would be far from ideal for any suitors, as they’d need to negotiate with the club rather than pursue a pre-contract move.

According to Tuttosport, via Goal, Juventus are beginning to express an interest in signing Bruno Fernandes next year, with his deal expiring in the summer.

Of course, they won’t be alone in that race, though. Indeed, Milan are believed to be in the mix too. He has a connection with Amorim and they share an agency, so logic would suggest that they may have the lead in any potential proceedings.

He’d also reportedly ‘welcome a return to Italy’ after his experiences with Novara, Udinese and Sampdoria. In something of a boost to their chances too, he has no interest in a move outside of Europe. Ruling out an exit to the MLS or Saudi Arabia.

Industry News: Tottenham transfer news: Spurs 'suffer blow' in midfielder pursuit

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Saikat Mandal | 26 Nov 2026 07:41.
  • Tottenham Hotspur may have suffered a setback in their pursuit of Inter Milan central midfielder Hakan Calhanoglu ahead of the January transfer window or next summer.
  • After enduring the worst possible start to the 2026-27 campaign, during which Spurs failed to win any of their opening seven games, they have bounced back strongly in the league.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 26 Nov 2026 07:41.

Tottenham Hotspur may have suffered a setback in their pursuit of Inter Milan central midfielder Hakan Calhanoglu ahead of the January transfer window or next summer.

After enduring the worst possible start to the 2026-27 campaign, during which Spurs failed to win any of their opening seven games, they have bounced back strongly in the league.

The north London club have picked up four wins in their last five matches, climbing to 10th in the Premier League table with 15 points, six adrift of fourth-placed Liverpool.

Spurs spent heavily to strengthen their midfield during the summer, bringing in Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes, but the club are still looking to add further quality in that department.

Recent reports have suggested that Tottenham have earmarked Calhanoglu as a target for next summer, although Galatasaray, Juventus and Como are also interested in the midfielder.

According to a report from Football Insider, Spurs may have suffered a blow in the race, with Calhanoglu preferring to remain at Inter Milan.

The 32-year-old midfielder is out of contract with the Italian giants at the end of the season, but preliminary talks have begun over an extension as he is keen to continue his career at San Siro.

Since joining from AC Milan in the summer of 2021, Calhanoglu has scored 53 goals in 226 appearances for the Nerazzurri.

The central midfielder registered 19 goal contributions in 30 games last term and has already scored three goals in his opening 10 league appearances this season.

While Spurs can match Calhanoglu's wage demands, they are not prepared to pay a transfer fee at this stage, instead hoping to sign him on a free transfer.

This leaves Tottenham anxiously waiting to see whether the Turkish midfielder can reach an agreement with Inter over a fresh deal.

Calhanoglu can operate as a defensive midfielder and is renowned for his excellent long-range shooting, making him an exciting potential addition to De Zerbi's squad, even at this stage of his career.

#142068. Clinical landscape of cardiometabolic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 35m • 📚 Deep Dive (6952 w)

Clinical landscape of cardiometabolic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 35 min read (6952 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~35 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) has emerged as the predominant form of heart failure worldwide and is increasingly associated with obesity, type 2 diabetes and systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) has emerged as the predominant form of heart failure worldwide and is increasingly associated with obesity, type 2 diabetes and systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction. This cardiometabolic HFpEF entity can be conceptualized as a mechanistically defined endotype marked by endothelial dysfunction, metabolic inflexibility and maladaptive inter-organ signalling involving the liver, kidney, adipose tissue and skeletal muscle. The cardiometabolic endotype often corresponds to a clinically recognizable adiposity-related clinical phenotype. Despite the growing prevalence of cardiometabolic HFpEF, therapeutic progress has lagged. This is mostly because the classification structure used is based on a commonly over-interpreted biomarker—ejection fraction—although inadequate trial end points and a lack of mechanism-guided precision also have a role. Here we review the evolving epidemiology, mechanistic underpinnings and emerging therapeutic landscape of cardiometabolic HFpEF. We highlight limitations in current diagnostic criteria, the role of extracardiac drivers and the need for soft end points and systems-based modelling. Advances in '-omics', phenotyping and cross-disciplinary frameworks now offer a pathway towards mechanistically targeted interventions that could enable symptomatic control by modifying validated disease mechanisms that culminate in this syndrome.

Harry Kane proves there is only one Ballon d’Or winner

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that arsenal would have deservedly won this Champions League match away to Bayern Munich if Kane was not on the pitch.
  • A brilliantly worked team-goal finished off by Declan Rice, and Arsenal are level 💥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/Y25zI80A0z.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that let’s cut to the chase. If there is any justice, sanity or logic in football then Harry Kane will win the Ballon d’Or when the ceremony takes place in London on Monday.

Industry observers note that arsenal would have deservedly won this Champions League match away to Bayern Munich if Kane was not on the pitch. Instead, they almost lost it but for another bit of brilliance from Declan Rice, Kane’s vice-captain for England, and probably his successor to wear the armband.

A brilliantly worked team-goal finished off by Declan Rice, and Arsenal are level 💥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/Y25zI80A0z.

“I’m lucky I can play with him and not so lucky I have to play against him,” Rice said, and that summed it up succinctly.

It has been revealed that and that Ballon d’Or? There is bias, but Rice – who is also on the 30-strong list of nominees – added of Kane: “He is the clear winner. His numbers speak for themselves, the year he has had has been remarkable. When you play with him you realise how good he is and when you play against him you see how much of a pain it is.”.

Industry observers note that arsenal stood toe-to-toe with Bayern in an open match. Both sides went for it, partly because they knew under the Champions League format, that defeat was not a disaster. There has been some chat about whether Arsenal can be, well, a bit dull. Not here. It would be no surprise to see these two face off again deep into this competition.

According to recent reports, the only setback for Arsenal was a worrying injury to Bukayo Saka early on, limping off and tapping his thigh, indicating an issue with his muscle. Mikel Arteta’s reaction betrayed his understandable concern.

Kane won a penalty and then expertly took it to give Bayern the lead. Other strikers could have scored the penalty but few would have created the wonderful assist that drew Bayern level.

It has been a fact for quite some years that Kane is not only the best goalscorer for England but the best passer. Indeed, if Kane could provide for Kane he would have scored even more goals.

“Unsere nummer neun,” shouted the stadium announcer after Kane’s goal and that needed no translation. Kane is a god in Bavaria, where they know a few things about having great centre-forwards. But the 33-year-old is surpassing them all.

Kane’s goal meant he had scored in 10 straight Champions League games, one short of the record held by Cristiano Ronaldo. It was also the former Tottenham Hotspur forward’s 16th goal in 23 games against Arsenal. No one has ever scored more against them.

Recent findings suggest that kane is the complete player, carrying out his defensive duties – winning headers to clear Bayern’s lines from Arsenal free-kicks – to linking the play to being the focus of his team’s attacks. He is a centre-half, central midfielder and centre-forward. Who pops up on the wing to deliver pinpoint crosses.

Maybe Kane will be pipped at the Palladium – the theatre where the ceremony takes place – by Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal or Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé, or even an absurd sympathy vote for Lionel Messi. But Kane deserves it. His time is now.

Some passages of play in the first half deserve analysis. Just to highlight how good Kane was. After an Arsenal corner, wastefully volleyed over by Riccardo Calafiori, Bayern countered and suddenly it was three on two. Serge Gnabry, the former Arsenal winger, had to do better than shoot weakly when picked out on the overlap. David Raya saved. That was a let-off.

According to recent reports, but who sprung that counter? It was not Manuel Neuer, the Bayern goalkeeper, taking the goal-kick, but Kane, with his sharp thinking. And then Kane introduced a superb pass from deep which Ismael Saibari should have dealt with better. It should have been another opportunity. Potentially a goal.

Is there anything Harry Kane can't do? 🧐 His goal kick very nearly led to a Bayern Munich goal 😲 https://t.co/fqbsN7KOjw.

In a recent development, and then Bayern did score. The ball was played inside to Kane, in centre field and afforded too much space. He delivered a perfectly weighted through ball for Alphonse Davies to run on to. The pace was perfect, allowing the Canadian not to break stride and stroke it past Raya. Kane did not fire the ball in, he did not make Davies work to reach it and he did not give Jurrien Timber any chance of cutting it out. It was perfect. Few players could do that. “Harry Kane puts the ball in a space from 30 metres that doesn’t exist,” Arteta mentioned. True.

Harry Kane with an OUTRAGEOUS assist, and Alphonso Davies equalises 🥵 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/6cGXrUloHW.

It was Saka’s replacement who gave Arsenal the lead, Eberechi Eze profiting from Martin Odegaard’s perceptive, lofted pass and taking advantage of Bayern’s ragged defending and some suspect goalkeeping from 40-year-old Neuer to score from an angle. Initially it was ruled out for offside, but that was overturned after a VAR check to provide Eze with a bit of redemption after being hooked against Nottingham Forest at the weekend.

VAR has given it, and Eze strikes Arsenal into the lead at the Allianz 🔥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/i1LjrZVnbI.

Neuer had his own slice of redemption as he saved well from Bruno Guimarães’ close-range header, pushing it against a post with Raya also excelling to beat out another header, this time from Dayot Upamecano.

Industry observers note that when Timber was punished for handball, as he blocked Kane’s shot, the penalty was given. Up stepped Kane and we knew the rest. At that point it felt like Bayern would win, but Arsenal continued to play courageously and pushed on, as they had done throughout, risking conceding further goals.

Harry Kane, what a penalty 🥶 He scores in his TENTH consecutive Champions League game to give Bayern the lead 😳 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/4k4jPCQEWF.

They were rewarded as Rice started the move, playing the ball in swiftly to Noni Madueke with substitute Viktor Gyokeres laying it back into the midfielder’s path. He strode on and Neuer was again beaten from an angle. It was certainly warranted, even if it did not detract from Kane’s night. But will he have a greater one on Monday?

Recent findings suggest that it had similarities [with last year’s league phase game]. I think we managed to create more chances but I think that Arsenal – and it’s something that has been mentioned by them before the game – they’ve worked a lot on retaining the ball and making it difficult to get the ball back. We did feel that.

It was a game in chunks. They had moments, we had moments. In our moments, I think we exploited the spaces in behind a little bit better maybe but we played against a top team and the result is a result between two massive teams.

Last year they reaped the benefits of a top-two finish: home ties all the way to the final and a guarantee of avoiding the other club in the top two.

They have a chance to pick off Real Madrid at the Emirates, and will anticipate Aston Villa (who still have to play Barcelona and PSG) and Real Betis dropping points.

Given PSG have already dispatched Manchester City and Barcelona, it is hard to envisage them dropping a point, though they do have the odd off night.

Arsenal’s chances of grabbing second could come down to winning their remaining games and Liverpool slipping up. But with five games to go, these permutations are probably premature.

Wow, what a game. That is one of the highest levels that we have played. The level of opposition, what the game required, and our level as well. Two teams who wanted to press each other and wanted to attack and wanted to play. It was a fascinating game.

In a recent development, I think we started the game incredibly well, we were so dominant, we did everything to deserve the first goal. We didn’t score the goal and lost Bukayo and had to adapt to it.

We gave a terrible chance away after our corner which could have cost us, then we scored the goal. In the second half, the game was even,  they started probably a little bit better before they scored and they you have to react and we certainly did.

The spirit of the team, the quality we have revealed on the second goal as well.

They are a bit concerned. A player having to come off with a sharp pain is never good news but we have to wait and see.

For me he’s the clear winner, his numbers speak for themselves. He’s obviously up against some other world class players. When you play with him you see how good it is, and when you play against him you see how much of a pain he is! As a striker to play that pass for the goal... he’s ridiculous. Lucky I can play with him, not so lucky when I have to play against him.

According to recent reports, I thought it was a good performance. Probably the draw was a fair result overall. We probably just didn’t get quite enough right tonight to get the win.

Nice to get the assist to get back into the game and then I thought we had some good moments but not enough over the 90 minutes.

It has been revealed that when you play against teams like Bayern who are man to man all over the pitch you have to apply certain principles, and I just kept running and managed to get away from my man. When they are following you all over, I just kept running and I was in on the goal.

According to recent reports, he’s been making such a good impact from the bench [Gyokeres]. He’s made some great runs tonight and set me up for the goal. When you play against man to man, who follow you everywhere over the whole pitch, it’s such a tough game. You have to apply certain principles and concepts, and you’re constantly thinking about where the space is. For the goal, Noni one-touch set, Viktor’s one-touch set, those little movements put you through on goal.

In periods of the game, it felt like Arsenal were trying to play in the manner of Bayern or PSG by leaving themselves so light at the back with acres of green grass to cover.

According to recent reports, would they play like that in a quarter-final? Probably not, and they were emboldened by Bayern missing some key players. But it helped them create danger and have some strong spells, even if there were some scary moments going the other way.

Somewhere between that display and Arsenal’s rearguard in the Champions League final is probably the sweet spot.

A high-quality game between two of the most plausible winners of this season’s Champions League finishes level.

It was a helter-skelter contest at times. For all the talk of Arteta being a conservative coach, Arsenal committed numbers forward in their press and when they attacked, and that left them vulnerable to Bayern’s fast transitions and Kane’s passes from deep.

Perhaps it is a missed opportunity to beat Bayern in the Allianz, given the German side started without Olise, Kimmich, Musiala and Diaz, but a point from the hardest fixture of the league phase is more than acceptable.

The fly in the ointment is the injury suffered by Saka in the first half, but Eze and Madueke performed well in his absence.

Just one minute to play and Bayern have the ball in Arsenal’s half, but Calafiori gets his foot in. Madueke does well to keep it and Lewis-Skelly finds Eze.

According to recent reports, timber with dig from outside the box after a poor defensive header from Bayern, and Neuer tips it over. Rice to take the corner, and Arsenal’s set-pieces have caused problems throughout. This might just be Arsenal’s chance to win it.

Swung to the back post, but Tah did enough.

According to recent reports, bayern had an injury worry of their own now: Luis Diaz, not judged fit to start, has pulled up and will have to come off. Bayern were in a promising position in the Arsenal half.

Three minutes of added time to play.

Harry Kane looking for another of those arced passes forward, but Eze read it and retrieved. Arsenal finishing the stronger when it comes to possession and territory. Perhaps that Premier League intensity bearing fruit as the game progresses.

A couple of fouls given away by both teams, it has been a bitty few minutes. But Arsenal do well to find Lewis-Skelly free in the middle of the pitch, and he finds Rice who drives the away team forward.

Neither team appears inclined to settle for the draw, but Arsenal have the wind in their sails. Mikel Merino is on for Martin Odegaard, who has probably been Arsenal’s best player on the night.

Arsenal back level again, and it is an emphatic finish across Neuer from Rice, after a deft touch from Gyokeres around the corner at the edge of the box. Bright football around the box from Arsenal. Still 10 minutes or so to play.

In a recent development, arsenal have been scoring gorgeous team goals all season. They have done so in all three of their Champions League games this season. They were labelled as “boring” after the Forest victory but that game was the exception, rather than the rule, on the evidence of this campaign.

A brilliantly worked team-goal finished off by Declan Rice, and Arsenal are level 💥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/Y25zI80A0z.

In a recent development, arsenal deep in Bayern territory after Rice’s cross towards Eze glanced off the head of a defender. Bayern are keeping a good defensive shape though, Arsenal finding it difficult to penetrate. Arteta is preparing another pair of changes.

According to recent reports, luis Diaz with a snap shot that brings a sharp save from David Raya. On the balance of chances and threat created, Bayern have earned their lead. But still plenty of football to play. Arsenal have not scored from a set-piece this season, but they have looked dangerous tonight. They need another couple.

Neuer has just smashed into Stanisic, sweeping up a long ball Timber was chasing.

Sources indicate that with Tzolis out and Saka now likely to be joining him on the sidelines, at what point does Arteta turn to Dowman in the league and Champions League? Obviously there are so many physical and defensive demands that are very difficult for a 16-year-old to meet... but the talent is there.

Arsenal enjoying plenty of territory and possession now, but you’d say Bayern look more likely to score on the counter-attack. Arsenal content to keep the ball and set themselves for a late assault.

In a recent development, lewis-Skelly with a no-touch turn in midfield but then he takes too long and Bischof wins the ball cleanly. Davies nutmegs Rice on the counter, but Madueke tracked back diligently to snuff out the danger. At the other end, Karl fouls Eze who has enjoyed a strong game, aside from his goal.

Vincent Kompany is in the building. It wasn’t clear whether the Bayern head coach would be able to attend tonight’s game because he’s been battling a nasty virus over the last few days. He did not do the usual pre-match press conference yesterday but clearly feels well enough to be here tonight.

Sam writes: “Arteta also did not have a coaching staff assembled. Arsenal: The Inside Story of Arsenal’s Rebirth Under Mikel Arteta (Pan Macmillan, RRP £22).

This is a proper heavyweight clash but, sadly for the neutrals watching, Bayern are missing some big players. Michael Olise is suspended, Jamal Musiala is injured and Joshua Kimmich is unavailable following the death of his father.

This should all work in Arsenal’s favour, and Mikel Arteta will be looking for a repeat of the energy and quality that his team demonstrated against Bayern last season. Arsenal won 3-1 at the Emirates in November in a performance of real class. It was arguably their most complete showing of the entire campaign.

Ice cold from Martinelli 🥶 https://t.co/uQEHb4x7eH.

Industry observers note that some excellent, if disquieting, detail from Sam Dean in this piece about the mood around Arsenal away from the first-team following the news of 60 planned redundancies. Sam writes that there are expecting to be other experienced and influential figures departing. The timing of cuts invites particular scrutiny, coming after the emotional peak of winning the league, record revenues and Mikel Arteta’s new contract.

After Arsenal were beaten by Bayern Munich in a Champions League quarter-final two years ago, Mikel Arteta bemoaned a lack of “magic moments” in attack.

Arsenal have since progressed to a Champions League semi-final and final, while ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title.

The upward trajectory has translated to tangible success, but Arsenal are still searching the level-raising attacker they lacked on their last visit to the Allianz Arena in 2024.

Back then, Arsenal’s offensive game revolved around Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard and that remains the case, which makes one wonder if Arsenal’s forward options have been adequately renewed.

A pair of stodgy performances (in victory) against Leeds United and Nottingham Forest have amplified those questions, though some of Arsenal’s slicker football in the season’s early weeks has been forgotten a little hastily.

They have made another strong start to another European campaign with six points from six, but this is undoubtedly their hardest fixture of the league phase.

Their chances of matching last season’s eight wins from eight could well hinge on the outcome of tonight’s game, but there are worse times to face Bayern.

Vincent Kompany’s team looks as formidable as ever, having scored 22 goals from six Bundesliga games so far this season. Their rotational approach is hard to track, with runners from deep breaking beyond Harry Kane who wanders into deep midfield positions.

However, they are without Michael Olise (suspension) and Jamal Musiala (injury) while Joshua Kimmich will miss the game on compassionate grounds following the death of his father.

With the exception of William Saliba, Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincacpie, Arsenal have a pretty clean bill of health and the strength of their bench was crucial against Leeds, Lille and Forest last week.

For Arteta, there are some interesting selection calls to make. It is anticipated that Jurrien Timber will replace Ben White at right-back, and first-choice left-back Riccardo Calafiori has been rested for the Champions League games so far. Should Arteta continue that policy, Myles Lewis-Skelly will fill the position, which will likely mean a midfield start for Bruno Guimarães or Mikel Merino.

Arsenal’s manager must also decide between Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze on the left, and Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz up front. Havertz is Arteta’s preference, but he also has to consider a relatively short turnaround before Saturday’s league game against Everton.

The eight players that should be on Man United's January list to turn season around - even with paltry £50m budget: From a goalscorer available for just £7m to star desperate to reunite with Mauricio Pochettino and a flying left back

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Inside the corridors of power at Manchester United, there is not the same appetite for a January splurge as there is among the club's fanbase.
  • While the winter transfer window brings hope for supporters desperate to see the mistakes of the summer rectified, United's decision-makers are anticipating a far more modest outlay.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 24 November 2026.

Inside the corridors of power at Manchester United, there is not the same appetite for a January splurge as there is among the club's fanbase.

While the winter transfer window brings hope for supporters desperate to see the mistakes of the summer rectified, United's decision-makers are anticipating a far more modest outlay.

As exclusively revealed by Daily Mail Sport, United strategy to spend less than £50million, with two additions targeted, one of which could be on loan.

Should United, at the moment 19th, remain in the bottom three by the time the window opens on January 1, there is a slim chance they go big in a desperate bid to guarantee their Premier League status.

But for now, the watchword inside United is discipline, and that means any recruitment will have to be more creative than ever before.

Here Daily Mail Sport looks at the transfer landscape and assesses eight players – a mix of Premier League proven and some lesser-known quantities – who could fit United’s needs AND their budget….

Mauricio Pochettino needs recruits in January - although Man United's budget being below £50m won't help his cause.

Brentford centre back Nathan Collins is one of United's top targets, but he won't be available on the cheap.

Position: Centre back, Age: 25, Club: Brentford.

Signing Premier League proven players is absolutely the preference of the United hierarchy, as evidenced by their recent business. Six of their past eight arrivals joined with experience in the division under their belt.

Collins is one of the club’s top targets for the winter window. The 25-year-old Brentford captain would bring leadership, an aerial presence and is comfortable as a ball carrier from the back, which Pochettino values.

According to recent reports, collins is seen as having many of the same attributes that Harry Maguire has brought to United over the years. And while he is not a flash name, he is viewed as a player that can immediately deliver some solidity.

Highly durable and a threat at set-pieces, Brentford won’t be willing to part with their captain, who is under contract until 2029, on the cheap.

Signing Collins would eat up most of the budget – but United are not deterred.

Position: Left back, Age: 25, Club: Man City.

United made a late play to land the Algerian on loan in January, only for City to tell them they would only sanction a permanent exit. In the end, time ran out and Ait-Nouri stayed put.

He has started just one game in all competitions under Enzo Maresca and is yet to feature at all in the Premier League this season. His situation is unlikely to improve in the near future, either.

A loan with an obligation to buy could suit all parties here, even if sending Ait-Nouri to their fiercest rivals may be difficult for City to stomach.

It has been revealed that rayan Ait-Nouri (right) has fallen out of favour under Enzo Maresca and is yet to play a minute in the Premier League this season. Could he make a move across Manchester?

Position: Left back, Age: 27, Club: Crystal Palace.

An intriguing option given United have been keeping tabs on Mitchell for over a year.

Palace are quite secretive when it comes to Mitchell – they kept his last contract extension under wraps – but as it stands, his deal is set to expire at the end of the season.

In a recent development, mitchell has the stamina to cope with Pochettino’s style of play and what he lacks in end product, he makes up for with his relentless pressing and recovery pace. The same is true of Fulham's Calvin Bassey, but sources are increasingly sceptical about United's chances of signing him in January.

For all of Palace’s struggles, Mitchell is proven at this level and would likely hit the ground running. The fact United are not his only suitor is a sign they aren’t straying down a blind alley.

With the 27-year-old’s contract yet to be extended and big clubs sniffing around, he could prove to be this January’s Marc Guehi should United nip in ahead of Liverpool, with Reds boss Andoni Iraola also keen.

Tyrick Mitchell has the stamina to cope with Pochettino’s style of play and what he lacks in end product, he makes up for with his relentless pressing and recovery pace.

Position: Forward, Age: 29, Club: Tottenham.

Out of favour under Roberto De Zerbi, Richarlison could help Tottenham Hotspur, Manchester United and himself in one fell swoop.

It has been revealed that in the summer, Spurs were looking for £20m for the Brazilian. Now the feeling is they would take a figure below £10m – some sources think £7m may suffice – to move on a player who has been kicking his heels since playing for the Under 21s away to Cheltenham Town in October.

Richarlison saw summer offers from Everton, Trabzonspor and Vasco da Gama fall through for various reasons and with United desperate to bolster their front line, this one could suit all parties. Richarlison is a strong presser from the front, versatile and better in the air than he is perhaps given credit for. He’s also no stranger to football's dark arts, something Pochettino appreciates.

The 29-year-old would offer a greater goal threat than Joshua Zirkzee, who saw moves of his own collapse in the summer, and showed last season what a threat he can be, scoring 11 league goals.

Spurs just want him out of the building and while that is normally a red flag, United need all the help they can get in a difficult market.

Richarlison is available for a bargain fee in January - even if he comes with some red flags attached.

Position: Centre back, Age: 28, Club: AC Milan.

United have rarely gone to the continent for recruits in recent seasons. But their limited budget makes Premier League players extremely difficult to acquire.

One option who might be available for a bargain fee is AC Milan's Fikayo Tomori, who is out of contract in the summer. The expectation in Milan is that Tomori will be moved on in January, allowing former United boss Ruben Amorim to add to his defence.

Tomori was initally frozen out by Amorim – he’d have a good ice-breaker should he pitch up at United! – and was even stripped of a squad number, before he was gradually reintroduced.

The England international has started just four games this season – only two in the league – and while Tomori has limitations in the air, he would bring Premier League experience and a level of leadership that is sorely lacking. His ability to bring the ball out and into midfield would make him a regular starter in Manchester.

When Milan won Serie A in 2022, Tomori was aggressive in his press and indicated he could play on either side as a centre back, and also slot in at right back when required.

Milan want to sell him, United need defensive reinforcements, and a cut-price deal suits everyone. This one is a no-brainer, thanks to Amorim of all people.

Fikayo Tomori looks set to move on from AC Milan in January with former United boss Ruben Amorim keen to shuffle his defensive pack.

Position: Left back/centre back, Age: 29, Club: Stuttgart.

An experienced option that could cover multiple positions across the back line, Mittelstadt would prove really shrewd business.

Under contract until 2028, the player has not agitated for a move but sources in Germany have indicated no extension talks are underway at this stage.

Stuttgart are eighth in the Bundesliga and should European football start to look out of reach, a sale of someone like Mittelstadt may become a necessity.

In a recent development, united should look at him even though his resale value would be limited, as he would immediately bring experience and quality. Mittelstadt, who was Germany's first-choice left back at Euro 2024, is a proactive defender that doesn’t shirk challenges and his durability means United could count on him from the off – vital given their lack of high-quality options at left back.

Signing Mittelstadt would go against everything the club's executives want to do – but they demonstrated by bringing in the 29-year-old Youri Tielemans in the summer that they are prepared to make exceptions on some older players.

Germany international Maximilian Mittelstadt (right) would add quality at full back.

Position: Left back, Age: 23, Club: Real Madrid.

Carreras should never have been allowed to leave United, but now comes a chance to rectify the mistake the club made in letting him go two-and-a-half years ago.

The 23-year-old has not been a regular starter under Jose Mourinho at Real Madrid and a player of his undoubted quality won't be happy with that state of affairs.

Real don’t need to cut their losses on a young player who is contracted through to 2031, which is exactly why Pochettino should go to Mourinho and see if he can take Carreras on loan for the rest of the season.

He is a better creator of chances than Patrick Dorgu or Luke Shaw and while Dorgu offers greater threat in the final third, Carreras feels a more well-rounded option at left back that is a better match-up against the league’s top wingers.

Carreras needs regular starts to develop and here is a chance for Mourinho to do his former side a favour when they are cash-strapped.

United made a mistake in letting Alvaro Carreras (right) go in 2024 - now it is time to rectify it.

Folarin Balogun forged a strong connection with Pochettino with the US national team and looks set to leave Monaco in the near future.

Position: Forward, Age: 25, Club: Monaco.

A striker that looked bound for Everton until a last-minute, deadline-day U-turn in the summer, it is widely known among recruitment staff that Balogun is available in January.

The Arsenal academy graduate has worked under Pochettino extensively with the US national team and, having had a reduced role at Monaco since the botched Everton move, a fresh start under a manager who knows how to get the best out of him would suit everyone.

Sources indicate that ‘There were just floods (of tears) from many people, but it's bound to happen,’ noted Balogun when Pochettino left the USA job. ‘We had a really close relationship, him, his staff and us as players. We were really connected. It was always going to be a sad goodbye for that reason.’.

According to recent reports, pochettino and Balogun's desire to reunite will be strong, but money could be an issue here. A loan with a conditional obligation to buy could be the best compromise, with incentives based on United's league position or Balogun's goals scored.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 26 Nov 2026 08:21.

Manchester United reportedly remain open to selling Marcus Rashford in January if they receive a suitable offer for the forward.

Rashford spent last season on loan at Barcelona, and it appeared that his future lay away from Old Trafford after he fell out with former manager Ruben Amorim.

Man Utd publicly backed his reintegration into the squad after Barcelona opted against signing him permanently, but the England international has so far cut a disappointing figure.

Rashford has made six Premier League appearances this season, starting four of them, but is yet to register a goal or assist.

With Mauricio Pochettino looking to reshape the attacking line-up in his own image, Rashford could once again find himself facing an uncertain future.

Speaking on the Market Madness podcast, transfer expert Ben Jacobs has suggested that the Red Devils would still consider suitable offers for Rashford.

The forward remains under contract at United until 2028, meaning the club are under no immediate pressure to sell him.

At the same time, the Red Devils could consider letting him leave as they look to add depth and quality to their forward department in January or potentially next summer.

Rashford is presently sidelined with a hip injury and missed both of Pochettino's first two games in charge. However, the club expect him to return before the end of the month, potentially in time for the clash against Brentford.

Joshua Zirkzee came on at half-time against Liverpool, but there is a strong possibility that the Dutch striker could be offloaded, with several Serie A clubs reportedly keen on his signature.

Pochettino also needs to reshape his defence, with signing a fresh centre-back a priority, potentially putting Lisandro Martinez's future at the club in doubt.

There are also doubts over the long-term future of captain Bruno Fernandes, who has already rejected two contract offers from the club.

By Ben Knapton | 26 Nov 2026 08:36.

Seeking to surge nine points clear of Manchester City at the top of the Premier League table, Arsenal welcome Enzo Maresca's men to the Emirates Stadium for Sunday's main event.

The Gunners were not punished for dropping points in their 2-2 draw with Newcastle United last weekend, thanks to the Sky Blues' own slip-up against Fulham and Brighton & Hove Albion's shock loss at Hull City.

The champions therefore sit six points clear of both blue-clad rivals after 11 matches, but the Emirates faithful experienced draw deja vu in Tuesday's 1-1 stalemate with Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up all of Arsenal's latest injury and suspension news for their clash with Man City, who also had to settle for a point in Europe last time out, being held to a 2-2 draw at home to Napoli.

In a recent development, possible return date: November 29 (vs. Manchester City).

David Raya appeared to have done serious damage to his shoulder when he was taken off against Newcastle, but Arsenal's number one has avoided a major injury and will not require surgery.

Arteta has not ruled him out of Sunday's game just yet, but he is facing a race against time to prove his fitness.

Recent findings suggest that possible return date: December 20 (vs. Manchester United).

Bukayo Saka suffered a severe quadriceps injury in October's 2-2 Champions League draw with Bayern Munich, and the England international will not return to action until just before Christmas in the best-case scenario.

In a recent development, possible return date: December 20 (vs. Manchester United).

Martin Zubimendi pulled his hamstring during Spain's Nations League defeat to England earlier this month, and like Saka, the midfielder faces another few weeks in the medical bay.

Arsenal have no players suspended for this game, as Max Dowman has now completed a three-match ban following his red card against Fleetwood Town in the EFL Cup.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 26 Nov 2026 08:54.

On the hunt for a fifth win in six Premier League matches, Tottenham Hotspur head north to battle Sunderland at the Stadium of Light on Sunday afternoon.

Roberto De Zerbi's men consigned their Leeds United loss to the past last weekend, easing past Ipswich Town 2-0 courtesy of goals from young star Luca Williams-Barnett and Dominic Solanke.

The Lilywhites have returned to the top half of the Premier League table as a result, and De Zerbi now seeks a slice of revenge after suffering a 1-0 defeat to Sunderland in his Tottenham debut last season.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up all of Tottenham's latest injury and suspension news ahead of their meeting with the Black Cats, who are 18th in the rankings with nine points from 11 games.

In a recent development, possible return date: November 29 (vs. Sunderland).

Sandro Tonali was absent from last Saturday's win over Ipswich due to illness, but he has returned to Tottenham training and is expected to be available for the weekend.

Savio returned from a muscular injury as a second-half substitute against Ipswich, but the Brazilian attacker then had to come off with a similar problem towards the end.

The severity of Savio's latest concern is not clear, but there is little to no chance of him facing Sunderland.

Possible return date: November 29 (vs. Sunderland).

Tosin Adarabioyo had made a full recovery from a calf injury before last weekend's triumph, but he was not risked by De Zerbi.

However, if the defender can prove his fitness this week, he should be in the matchday squad at the Stadium of Light.

Possible return date: December 6 (vs. Arsenal).

Chelsea loanee Mykhaylo Mudryk is still on the mend from an ankle injury, and the Ukrainian is not expected to return to action for another couple of weeks.

According to recent reports, possible return date: February 20 (vs. Brighton & Hove Albion).

Xavi Simons is almost seven months into his recovery from an ACL rupture, and all being well, the Dutchman could make his comeback in mid to late February.

Possible return date: February 6 (vs. Ipswich Town).

Likewise, Wilson Odobert will not play again in 2026 due to his own serious knee injury, but De Zerbi is hopeful that the winger will return to full training in January ahead of a potential February return.

Sources indicate that possible return date: December 6 (vs. Arsenal).

De Zerbi revealed last week that Mathys Tel will need another "two or three weeks" to recover from the ankle injury he picked up against Leeds, so the Frenchman could be targeting a comeback for the North London derby on December 6.

Tottenham have no players banned for this game.

It seems we are heading into the final year of Fikayo Tomori’s playing relationship with AC Milan, with talk of a renewal silent.

Next year, at the end of June, Tomori’s deal expires and if nothing is done before then, his six-year spell with the club will come to an end.

In a recent development, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

According to recent reports, it’s been an up-and-down season for the Englishman, especially after he was included in the ‘bomb squad’ through the mercato. However, he was needed back in the squad and reintegrated.

Despite showing this fight, though, it seems unlikely that he’ll be rewarded with a upcoming deal. There are plans to invest heavily in the club next year and the defender isn’t seen as a pillar of the team, let alone the defence. So a renewal isn’t being focused on.

As Matteo Moretto told viewers on Fabrizio Romano’s YouTube channel, Tomori previously had a chance at a renewal. However, that now seems to have gone, as MilanNews relays.

“There’s a before and after regarding Tomori. In my opinion, if Massimiliano Allegri had remained on the Milan bench, perhaps in that case there could have been a chance of a renewal for Tomori.

It has been revealed that “Then there was the slightly peculiar way Milan handled the Tomori situation. Tomori is a player who has always been absolutely professional and deeply loves the Milan shirt; he has always shown all his commitment.

According to recent reports, “It’s true, he was sidelined; Milan tried to find solutions on the way out right in the last days of the transfer window. His contract expires in 2027.

“There were discussions underway for the renewal when Allegri was on the bench; then, with time and with the succession of certain events, this type of renewal was no longer discussed.

“To date, the negotiations are absolutely at a standstill. There is no dialogue between the parties and I repeat, Tomori’s contract expires in 2027.

“We’ll see if in January there can be a way out, perhaps with the payment of compensation to Milan, or if it will reach zero in June, but as of today there is no trace of a possible renewal.”.

#142032. Industry News: Structural basis of RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CAST systems
